title.zh: 卷279 列傳六十六 杨方兴 朱之锡 靳辅 于成龙 张鹏翮
title.en: Volume 279 Biographies 66: Yang Fangxing, Zhu Zhixi, Jin Fu, Yu Chenglong, Zhang Penghe
title.raw: 卷279 列傳六十六 杨方兴 朱之锡 靳辅 于成龙 张鹏翮

sentences.zh: 列傳六十六

translations.literal: Biographies 66
translations.idiomatic: Biography 66

sentences.zh: 楊方興硃之錫崔維雅靳輔陳潢宋文運董訥熊一瀟

translations.literal: Yang Fangxing, Zhu Zhixi, Cui Weiya, Jin Fu, Chen Huang, Song Wenyun, Dong Ne, and Xiong Yixiao
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fangxing, Zhu Zhixi, Cui Weiya, Jin Fu, Chen Huang, Song Wenyun, Dong Ne, and Xiong Yixiao

sentences.zh: 於成龍孫在豐開音布張鵬翮

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong, Sun Zaifeng, Kaiyinbu, and Zhang Penghe
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong, Sun Zaifeng, Kaiyinbu, and Zhang Penghe

sentences.zh: 楊方興，字浡然，漢軍鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Yang Fangxing, courtesy name Boran, was a man of the Han Army Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fangxing, styled Boran, belonged to the Han Military Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初為廣寧諸生。

translations.literal: At first he was a licentiate in Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun as a local scholar in Guangning.

sentences.zh: 天命七年，太祖取廣寧，方興來歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianming, when the Taizu took Guangning, Fangxing came over to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianming (1622), after the Taizu captured Guangning, Fangxing defected to the Manchus.

sentences.zh: 太宗命直內院，與修太祖實錄。

translations.literal: The Taizong ordered him to serve in the Inner Court and to assist in compiling the Veritable Records of the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong assigned him to the Inner Court and had him help compile the Veritable Records of the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，試中舉人，授牛錄額真銜，擢內秘書院學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he passed the provincial examination, was granted the title of niru captain, and was promoted to academician of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde (1636) he passed the provincial examination, received the rank of niru captain, and was promoted to academician of the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，嘗醉後犯蹕，論死，上貰之，命斷酒。

translations.literal: By nature he was fond of wine; once, while drunk, he violated the imperial procession and was sentenced to death, but the emperor pardoned him and ordered him to abstain from alcohol.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to drink; once, drunk, he intruded upon the imperial procession—a capital offense—but the emperor spared him and forbade him wine.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從入關。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the court in entering the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi (1644) he accompanied the dynasty south through the Pass.

sentences.zh: 七月，授河道總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed Director-General of Rivers and Canals.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was made Director-General of Rivers and Canals.

sentences.zh: 李自成決河灌開封，其後屢決屢塞，賊勢浸張，土寇群起，兩岸防守久廢。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng had breached the Yellow River to flood Kaifeng; thereafter the river broke and was dammed again and again, rebel strength gradually grew, local bandits rose in groups, and defense along both banks had long been neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng had breached the Yellow River to inundate Kaifeng; afterward the river burst and was sealed repeatedly, rebel power steadily grew, local bandits swarmed, and dikes on both banks had long gone unmaintained.

sentences.zh: 伏秋汛發，北岸小宋口、曹家寨堤潰，河水漫曹、單、金鄉、魚台四縣，自蘭陽入運河，田產盡沒。

translations.literal: When the summer and autumn flood season came, the dikes at Xiaosongkou and Caojiazhai on the north bank gave way; the river spread over the four counties of Cao, Shan, Jinxiang, and Yutai, entered the Grand Canal from Lanyang, and farmland was entirely submerged.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the summer-autumn floods, the north-bank dikes at Xiaosongkou and Caojiazhai collapsed; the river inundated Cao, Shan, Jinxiang, and Yutai, poured from Lanyang into the Grand Canal, and crops were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 方興至官，遣兵捕治土寇，掃穴擒渠，乃疏請修築。

translations.literal: When Fangxing took office he sent troops to suppress the local bandits, swept their dens and captured their leaders, and then memorialized requesting repairs and construction.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Fangxing sent troops against the bandits, rooted out their lairs and seized their chiefs, then memorialized for dike works.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，河決流通集，分兩道入運河，運河受河水淀濁淤塞，下流徐、邳、淮、揚亦多衝決。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year the river broke at Liutongji and split into two channels entering the Grand Canal; the canal, receiving the muddy Yellow River water, silted up, and downstream in Xu, Pi, Huai, and Yang there were also many breaches.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year (1645) the river burst at Liutongji and split into two courses into the Grand Canal; the canal choked on the Yellow River’s muddy flow, and downstream Xu, Pi, Huai, and Yang suffered many breaks as well.

sentences.zh: 方興以防護無功自劾，上諭以殫力河防，不必引咎。

translations.literal: Fangxing impeached himself for ineffective protection of the works; the emperor instructed him to devote his full strength to river defense and told him he need not take blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing submitted a self-impeachment for failing to hold the defenses; the emperor told him to throw all his energy into river control and not to blame himself.

sentences.zh: 旋疏薦補管河道方大猷等。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he memorialized recommending Fang Dayou and others to fill posts in river administration.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized recommending Fang Dayou and others to fill river-administration posts.

sentences.zh: 四年，流通集決口將合，河下注湍激，又決汶上入獨山湖。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the breach at Liutongji was about to close, but the river’s downward rush was violent and turbulent, and it broke again at Wenshang, flowing into Dushan Lake.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1647), as the Liutongji breach neared closure, the river’s plunge grew fierce and it broke anew at Wenshang into Dushan Lake.

sentences.zh: 方興請修築通濟閘上下堤岸，並淮安東北蘇淤、馬羅等堤，又築江都、高郵諸石堤，流通集合口。

translations.literal: Fangxing requested repairs to the dikes above and below the Tongji Sluice, and also the dikes at Suyu, Maluo, and elsewhere northeast of Huai’an, and further the stone dikes at Jiangdu, Gaoyou, and other places, and the mouth where the channels united at Liutongji.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing asked to rebuild the dikes above and below Tongji Sluice, the Suyu and Maluo dikes northeast of Huai’an, the stone dikes at Jiangdu and Gaoyou, and the united mouth at Liutongji.

sentences.zh: 進兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: He was advanced to the rank of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the concurrent rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 七年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1650) he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 八月，河決荊隆口，南岸出單家寨，北岸出硃源寨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the river broke at Jinglongkou; on the south bank it issued at Danjiazhai, on the north bank at Zhuyuanzhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the river burst at Jinglongkou—southward at Danjiazhai, northward at Zhuyuanzhai.

sentences.zh: 南岸先合，河全注北岸，張秋以下堤盡潰，自大清河東入海。

translations.literal: The south-bank channel closed first; the whole river poured into the north-bank channel, and below Zhangqiu the dikes all collapsed; the river entered the sea eastward through the Daqing River.
translations.idiomatic: The south channel sealed first; the entire current swung to the north bank, dikes below Zhangqiu gave way, and the river ran east to sea by the Daqing River.

sentences.zh: 方興用大猷議，於上游築長縷堤遏其勢，复築小長堤塞決口，期半年蕆事。

translations.literal: Following Dayou’s plan, Fangxing built a long continuous dike upstream to check the current, and also built a shorter continuous dike to seal the breach, expecting to finish within half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Adopting Dayou’s plan, Fangxing built a long upstream dike to check the flood and a shorter dike to plug the breach, aiming to finish in six months.

sentences.zh: 九年，方興復乞休，不許。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Fangxing again requested retirement, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1652) Fangxing again asked to retire; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 大猷擢江南按察使，方興請以新銜管河務。

translations.literal: Dayou was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Jiangnan; Fangxing requested that he manage river affairs under his new title.
translations.idiomatic: Dayou was promoted surveillance commissioner of Jiangnan; Fangxing asked that he oversee river work in his new capacity.

sentences.zh: 九年，荊隆口工竟，方興疏言：「清口，淮、黃交匯，黃強淮弱，歲需疏濬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Jinglongkou works were completed; Fangxing memorialized, saying: “At Qingkou the Huai and Yellow Rivers meet; the Yellow is strong and the Huai weak, and dredging is needed every year.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, when the Jinglongkou project was done, Fangxing wrote: “At Qingkou the Huai and Yellow meet; the Yellow dominates the Huai, and the channel must be dredged yearly.

sentences.zh: 請於清江、通濟二閘適中處修復福興閘，啟一閉二，以時蓄洩。

translations.literal: I request that at a point midway between the Qingjiang and Tongji sluices the Fuxing Sluice be restored, opening one and closing two, so that water may be stored and released in season.”
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Fuxing Sluice be restored midway between Qingjiang and Tongji—one open, two closed—to regulate storage and release in season.”

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 給事中許作梅，御史楊世學、陳棐交章請勘九河故道，導河北流入海。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Xu Zuomei and the censors Yang Shixue and Chen Fei submitted successive memorials requesting a survey of the old courses of the Nine Rivers and diversion of the Yellow River northward to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Xu Zuomei and censors Yang Shixue and Chen Fei jointly urged surveying the Nine Rivers’ old channels and sending the Yellow River north to the sea.

sentences.zh: 方興言：「河古今同患，而治河古今異宜。

translations.literal: Fangxing said: “The river has been the same affliction in ancient and modern times, but the right way to control it differs between ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing replied: “The river has always been a scourge, but the right remedy changes with the age.

sentences.zh: 宋以前治河，但令赴海有路，可南亦可北。

translations.literal: Before the Song, in controlling the river one need only ensure a path to the sea—it could go south or north.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Song, control meant only giving the river a path to the sea—south or north would do.

sentences.zh: 元、明迄我清，東南漕運，自清口迄董家口二百餘裡，藉河為轉輸，河可南必不可北。

translations.literal: From the Yuan and Ming down to our Qing, grain transport for the southeast relied on the river for transshipment over more than two hundred li from Qingkou to Dongjiakou; the river may go south but must by no means go north.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan and Ming through our dynasty, southeastern grain transport for more than two hundred li from Qingkou to Dongjiakou depends on the river as a conveyor—the current may run south but must never turn north.

sentences.zh: 若欲尋禹舊跡，導河北行，無論漕運不通，恐決出之水東西奔盪，不可收拾。

translations.literal: If one wishes to follow Yu’s old traces and guide the river north, apart from the fact that grain transport would be cut off, I fear the water released in a breach would surge east and west and become unmanageable.
translations.idiomatic: To trace Yu’s ancient course and drive the river north would not only break the grain route; the flood would likely surge east and west beyond control.

sentences.zh: 勢須別築數千里長堤，較之增卑培薄，難易顯然。

translations.literal: One would have to build separate dikes thousands of li long—the difficulty compared with raising low sections and bolstering thin ones is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: It would require building thousands of li of new dikes—a far harder task than raising low banks and thickening weak ones.

sentences.zh: 且河挾沙以行，束之為一，則水急沙流；

translations.literal: Moreover the river carries sand as it flows; if confined to a single channel, the water is swift and the sand moves;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the river moves laden with silt; confine it to one channel and the current runs fast and sand stays suspended;

sentences.zh: 播之為九，則水緩沙壅。

translations.literal: if spread into nine channels, the water is slow and the sand silts up.
translations.idiomatic: split it into nine and the water slows and sand piles up.

sentences.zh: 數年後河仍他徙，何以濟運？

translations.literal: Within a few years the river would still shift elsewhere—how then could transport be maintained?
translations.idiomatic: In a few years the river would shift again—how would transport survive?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為河不能無決，決而不築，司河者之罪；

translations.literal: Your servant is of the view that the river cannot be without breaches; if it breaches and one does not build dikes, that is the fault of those in charge of the river;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that breaches are inevitable; failure to repair them is the river officials’ fault;

sentences.zh: 河不能無淤，淤而不濬，亦司河者之罪。

translations.literal: the river cannot be without silt; if it silts and one does not dredge, that too is the fault of those in charge of the river.
translations.idiomatic: silt is inevitable too; failure to dredge is likewise their fault.

sentences.zh: 若欲保其不決不淤，誰敢任之？

translations.literal: If one wishes to guarantee that it will neither breach nor silt, who would dare undertake that?
translations.idiomatic: But who would dare promise it would never breach or silt?

sentences.zh: 請敕下廷議，定畫一之規，屏二三之說，俾有所遵守。

translations.literal: I request that Your Majesty order deliberation at court, fix a uniform policy, and set aside conflicting proposals so that there may be something to follow.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the court settle one uniform policy, set aside rival schemes, and give us a rule to follow.”

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and the emperor warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，河決大王廟，距硃源寨口不遠。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the river broke at Dawangmiao, not far from the Zhuyuanzhai breach.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1653) the river burst at Dawangmiao, not far from the Zhuyuanzhai gap.

sentences.zh: 給事中周體觀劾方興治河罔效，方興疏辨，因請罷斥，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Zhou Tiguan impeached Fangxing for ineffective river control; Fangxing memorialized in defense and asked to be dismissed, but a gracious edict comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhou Tiguan charged Fangxing with futile river work; Fangxing defended himself and asked to be removed, but a gracious edict kept him in post.

sentences.zh: 十一年，給事中林起龍复劾方興侵蝕工需，累民捐費至六十餘萬；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the supervising secretary Lin Qilong again impeached Fangxing for embezzling project funds and pressing the people for contributions totaling more than six hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1654) supervising secretary Lin Qilong again accused Fangxing of skimming project funds and extorting over six hundred thousand taels from the people;

sentences.zh: 並劾大猷等姦貪不法。

translations.literal: he also impeached Dayou and others for wicked greed and lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: and charged Dayou and others with corruption and lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 上解方興任，命入都質對，起龍以誣譴，方興復任。

translations.literal: The emperor relieved Fangxing of his post and ordered him to the capital to answer the charges; Qilong was punished for false accusation, and Fangxing was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended Fangxing and summoned him to the capital; Qilong was punished for slander, and Fangxing was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 既，直隸總督李廕祖复劾大猷貪婪誤工，方興亦劾大猷，上以其不先舉發，切責之。

translations.literal: Afterward the Zhili governor-general Li Yizu again impeached Dayou for greed and bungling the works; Fangxing also impeached Dayou, and the emperor sharply rebuked him for not having reported this earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhili governor-general Li Yizu again impeached Dayou for greed and botched works; Fangxing joined the charge, but the emperor sharply rebuked him for not having exposed Dayou sooner.

sentences.zh: 給事中董篤行又劾方興徇庇，降級留任。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Dong Duxing again impeached Fangxing for favoritism and cover-up; he was demoted one grade but kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Dong Duxing then charged Fangxing with shielding Dayou; Fangxing was demoted a grade but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 十四年，乞休，上念其勞，以原官加太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he requested retirement; the emperor, mindful of his labors, granted him retirement with his original rank plus Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1657) he asked to retire; honoring his service, the court let him leave office as Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 方興還京師，所居僅蔽風雨，布衣蔬食，四壁蕭然。

translations.literal: When Fangxing returned to the capital his dwelling barely kept out wind and rain; he wore plain cloth and ate simple food, and his four walls were bare.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital Fangxing lived in a hut that barely kept out weather, dressed in coarse cloth, ate plainly, and owned almost nothing.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi he died, and funeral sacrifices and burial honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Kangxi (1665) and was granted state funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 硃之錫，字孟九，浙江義烏人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhixi, courtesy name Mengjiu, was a native of Yiwu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhixi, styled Mengjiu, was from Yiwu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi, he was made a bachelor of the Hanlin and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi (1646), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月，擢弘文院侍讀學士，四遷至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year he was promoted to reader-in-waiting of the Hongwen Academy, and after four further promotions reached vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eleventh year (1654) he became reader of the Hongwen Academy and rose through four promotions to vice minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十四年，楊方興乞休，上特擢之錫，以兵部尚書銜，總督河道，駐濟寧。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when Yang Fangxing requested retirement, the emperor specially promoted Zhixi with the rank of Minister of War as Director-General of Rivers and Canals, stationed at Jining.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1657), when Yang Fangxing retired, the emperor specially promoted Zhixi to river director-general with Minister of War rank, based at Jining.

sentences.zh: 十五年十月，河決山陽柴溝，建義、馬邏諸堤並溢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year the river broke at Chaigou in Shanyang; the dikes at Jianyi, Maluo, and elsewhere all overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year (1658) the river burst at Chaigou in Shanyang and dikes at Jianyi, Maluo, and elsewhere failed together.

sentences.zh: 之錫馳赴清江浦築戧堤，塞決口。

translations.literal: Zhixi hurried to Qingjiangpu to build spur dikes and seal the breach.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixi rushed to Qingjiangpu, built spur dikes, and closed the breach.

sentences.zh: 宿遷董家口為沙所淤，就舊渠迤東別開河四百丈通運道。

translations.literal: Dongjiakou in Suqian was silted by sand; following the old channel he opened a new river four hundred zhang to the east to connect with the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: Dongjiakou in Suqian had silted shut; he cut a new four-hundred-zhang channel east of the old course to restore the transport line.

sentences.zh: 十六年，條上治河諸事，言：「河南歲修夫役，近屢經奏減，宜存舊額。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he itemized various matters of river control, saying: “The annual corvée for Henan repairs has recently been repeatedly reduced by memorial; the old quotas should be kept.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1659) he listed river-policy measures: “Henan’s annual repair corvée has been cut repeatedly by memorial; the old quotas should stand.

sentences.zh: 明製，淮工兼用民修，宜復舊例。

translations.literal: Under the Ming system Huai works used civilian labor as well; the old practice should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, Huai works used civilian labor too; that practice should return.

sentences.zh: 揚屬運道與高、寶諸湖相通，淮屬運道為黃、淮交會，舊有各堤閘，宜擇要修葺。

translations.literal: The transport route in Yang prefecture connects with the lakes of Gaoyou and Baoying; the route in Huai prefecture is where the Yellow and Huai meet—there were various dikes and sluices that should be selectively repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Yang’s transport line links the Gaoyou and Baoying lakes; Huai’s line is where Yellow and Huai meet—key dikes and sluices there should be repaired.

sentences.zh: 應用柳料，宜令瀕河州縣預為籌備。

translations.literal: Willow materials that will be needed should be ordered prepared in advance by counties along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Willow materials should be stockpiled in advance by riparian counties.

sentences.zh: 姦豪包佔夫役，賣富僉貧，工需各物，私弊百出，宜責司、道、府、廳查報，徇隱者以溺職論。

translations.literal: Wicked powerful men monopolize corvée assignments, selling off duties from the rich to the poor; for all kinds of project supplies private abuses abound in hundreds of ways—circuit, prefectural, and subprefectural officials should be charged to investigate and report, and those who conceal offenses should be punished for dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Local bullies monopolize corvée, shifting burdens from rich to poor; project supplies breed endless private abuses—circuit, prefectural, and county officials must investigate and report; concealment should count as dereliction.

sentences.zh: 額設水夫，陰雨不赴工，所扣工食，謂之曠盡，宜令管河廳道嚴覈。

translations.literal: Established river laborers who fail to report in rainy weather have their rations deducted—this is called ‘total absence’—and river offices and circuit officials should be ordered to scrutinize this strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Registered boatmen who skip work in rain have rations docked as ‘total absence’; river offices and circuit officials must audit this strictly.

sentences.zh: 河員升調降用，宜令候代始行離任。

translations.literal: When river officials are promoted, transferred, demoted, or reassigned, they should be required to wait until their successors arrive before leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: River officials promoted, transferred, or demoted should not leave until their successors arrive.

sentences.zh: 河員有專責，不宜別有差委。

translations.literal: River officials have specialized duties and should not receive other assignments.
translations.idiomatic: River officers have sole charge and should receive no other assignments.

sentences.zh: 歲終察覈舉劾，並宜復舊例。

translations.literal: Year-end inspection with recommendations and impeachments should also be restored to the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Year-end review with recommendations and impeachments should likewise be restored.”

sentences.zh: 」皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All items were sent to the ministries for action.

sentences.zh: 之錫丁母憂，命在任守制，疏請歸葬，優詔給假治喪。

translations.literal: Zhixi entered mourning for his mother; he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office, memorialized to return home for burial, and received an excellent edict granting leave to conduct the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixi mourned his mother he was ordered to observe filial rites in post; he asked leave to bury her at home and received a gracious edict granting funeral leave.

sentences.zh: 十七年，還任。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1660) he resumed office.

sentences.zh: 以捐金賑淮、揚、徐三府災，加太子少保。

translations.literal: For contributing funds to relieve disaster in the three prefectures of Huai, Yang, and Xu, he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For donating relief funds to flood victims in Huai, Yang, and Xu, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，河決原武、祥符、蘭陽縣境，東溢曹縣，復決石香爐村。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi the river broke in the districts of Yuanwu, Xiangfu, and Lanyang, overflowed east into Cao county, and broke again at Shixianglu Village.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi (1662) the river burst in Yuanwu, Xiangfu, and Lanyang, flooded east into Cao county, and broke again at Shixianglu Village.

sentences.zh: 之錫檄濟寧道方兆及董曹縣役，而赴河南督塞西閻寨、單家寨、時利驛、蔡家樓、策家寨諸決口。

translations.literal: Zhixi dispatched orders to the Jining circuit intendant Fang Zhao and labor from Cao county to supervise work, while he himself went to Henan to oversee sealing the breaches at Xiyanzhai, Danjiazhai, Shiliyi, Caijialou, Cejiazhai, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixi ordered Jining intendant Fang Zhao and Cao county labor to manage local works while he went to Henan to oversee plugging Xiyanzhai, Danjiazhai, Shiliyi, Caijialou, Cejiazhai, and other breaches.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，疏言：「南旺為運河之脊，北至臨清，南至台莊，四十餘閘，全賴啟閉得宜。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year he memorialized, saying: “Nanwang is the backbone of the Grand Canal; from there north to Linqing and south to Taizhuang are more than forty sluices, all depending on proper opening and closing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year (1665) he wrote: “Nanwang is the spine of the Grand Canal; from Linqing north to Taizhuang south lie more than forty sluices, all depending on correct operation.

sentences.zh: 瀕河春常少雨，伏秋雨多，東省久旱，山泉小者多枯，大者已弱。

translations.literal: Along the river spring usually has little rain and the summer and autumn floods bring much rain; Shandong had long been dry, most small mountain springs had dried up, and even large ones had weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Springs along the line are usually dry; summer-autumn rains are heavy. Shandong’s long drought had dried most small springs and weakened the large ones.

sentences.zh: 若官船經閘，應閉者強之使開，洩水下注，則重運之在上者阻；

translations.literal: If when official grain boats pass a sluice that should be closed it is forced open and water is released downstream, then heavy transport above is blocked;
translations.idiomatic: If grain boats pass a sluice that should stay closed and it is forced open, water drains downstream and upstream heavy transport is blocked;

sentences.zh: 應開者強之使閉，留水待船，則重運之在下者又阻。

translations.literal: if one that should be open is forced closed to hold water for boats, then heavy transport below is again blocked.
translations.idiomatic: if a sluice that should open is forced shut to hold water, downstream heavy transport is blocked in turn.

sentences.zh: 乞飭各遵例禁。

translations.literal: I beg that all be ordered to observe the regulations as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: I beg strict enforcement of the regulations.”

sentences.zh: 」得旨，非奉極要差遣，擅行啟閉者，準參奏。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: except on the most urgent imperial commission, those who open or close sluices on their own authority may be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that unauthorized sluice operation, except on the most urgent imperial business, was grounds for impeachment.

sentences.zh: 八月，疏言：「部議停差北河、中河、南河、南旺、夏鎮、通惠諸分司，歸併地方官。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he memorialized, saying: “The ministry has proposed abolishing the separate offices for the North River, Middle River, South River, Nanwang, Xiazhen, and Tonghui and merging them with local officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he wrote: “The ministry proposes abolishing the North River, Middle River, South River, Nanwang, Xiazhen, and Tonghui sub-commissions and merging them with local officials.

sentences.zh: 臣維河勢變幻，工料紛繁，天時不齊，非水則旱，或綢繆幾先，或補葺事後，或張皇於風雨倉遽之際，或調劑於左右方圓之間。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the river’s force is changeable, materials and labor are manifold, and the seasons are uneven—now flood, now drought; sometimes one must prepare well in advance, sometimes repair afterward, sometimes act urgently in wind and rain, sometimes adjust among conflicting demands.
translations.idiomatic: I find the river’s behavior unpredictable, materials and labor complex, seasons uneven—flood or drought by turns—requiring foresight, after-the-fact repair, emergency action in storms, and constant adjustment among competing needs.

sentences.zh: 北河所轄三千餘裡，其間三十餘閘；

translations.literal: The North River office oversees more than three thousand li, with more than thirty sluices along the way;
translations.idiomatic: The North River commission oversees three thousand li and more than thirty sluices;

sentences.zh: 中河所轄黃、運兩河，董口尤運道咽喉，清黃交接，濁流易灌；

translations.literal: the Middle River office oversees the Yellow and Transport rivers; Dongkou especially is the throat of the transport route, where clear and muddy waters meet and turbid flow easily inundates;
translations.idiomatic: the Middle River oversees Yellow and Transport; Dongkou is the transport throat where clear and muddy waters meet and silty flow easily backs up;

sentences.zh: 南河所轄在淮、黃、江、湖之間，相距窵遠；

translations.literal: the South River office oversees the region between the Huai, Yellow, Yangtze, and lakes, with great distances between points;
translations.idiomatic: the South River spans Huai, Yellow, Yangtze, and lakes over vast distances;

sentences.zh: 南旺、泉源三百餘處，近者或出道隅，遠者偏藏僻壤；

translations.literal: at Nanwang are more than three hundred springs; some nearby issue at a roadside, others lie hidden in remote soil;
translations.idiomatic: Nanwang alone has three hundred-odd springs—some at roadsides, others hidden in remote ground;

sentences.zh: 夏鎮地屬兩省，鑿石通漕，形勢陡絕，節宣閘座，尤費經營；

translations.literal: Xiazhen’s territory belongs to two provinces; cutting rock to open the grain route, the terrain is steep and precipitous, and regulating sluices there is especially costly to manage;
translations.idiomatic: Xiazhen straddles two provinces; cutting rock for the grain route is steep work and sluice regulation there especially demanding;

sentences.zh: 通惠浮沙易淺，峻水易衝，塞決之役，歲歲有之。

translations.literal: Tonghui has floating sand that easily shoals and steep water that easily breaches; sealing breaches is a task every year.
translations.idiomatic: Tonghui silts easily, steep currents breach easily, and breach repair is annual work.

sentences.zh: 若云歸併府佐，則職微權輕，上下掣肘。

translations.literal: If merged with prefectural assistants, their posts would be minor and authority light, with superiors and subordinates hampering one another.
translations.idiomatic: Merging them into prefectural assistants would mean petty rank, weak authority, and constant interference.

sentences.zh: 至於地方監司，責以終年累月奔馳駐守，揆之事勢，萬萬不能。

translations.literal: As for local surveillance commissioners, to charge them with year-round rushing about and garrison duty—measured against the situation, this is utterly impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting local surveillance commissioners to camp on site year-round is utterly impossible.

sentences.zh: 分司與各道界壤迥不相同，應合而分：一閘座也，上流以為應閉，下流以為應開；

translations.literal: The boundaries of sub-commissions and circuit offices are quite different; what should be united is divided: at one sluice the upstream holds it should be closed while downstream holds it should be open;
translations.idiomatic: Sub-commissions and circuit boundaries do not align; what should be unified is split: at one sluice upstream says close while downstream says open;

sentences.zh: 一額夫也，在此則欲求多，在彼又復患少。

translations.literal: for one quota of laborers, here they wish for more while there they again complain of too few.
translations.idiomatic: for one labor quota, one side wants more men while the other complains of too few.

sentences.zh: 不但紛競日多，必致牽制誤事。

translations.literal: Not only would disputes grow daily, but obstruction would necessarily cause mistakes in the work.
translations.idiomatic: Disputes would multiply daily and mutual obstruction would ruin the work.

sentences.zh: 應請仍循舊制。

translations.literal: I request that the old system still be followed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the old system be kept.”

sentences.zh: 」得旨允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，卒。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the fifth year (1666).

sentences.zh: 直隸山東河南總督硃昌祚疏言：「之錫治河十載，綢繆旱溢，則盡瘁昕宵；

translations.literal: The governor-general of Zhili, Shandong, and Henan, Zhu Changzuo, memorialized, saying: “In ten years of river control Zhixi prepared for drought and flood and exhausted himself from dawn to night;
translations.idiomatic: Zhili-Shandong-Henan governor-general Zhu Changzuo wrote: “In ten years of river work Zhixi planned for drought and flood and wore himself out from dawn to night;

sentences.zh: 疏濬堤渠，則馳驅南北。

translations.literal: in dredging dikes and channels he rushed back and forth between north and south.
translations.idiomatic: in dredging dikes and channels he raced between north and south.

sentences.zh: 受事之初，河庫貯銀十餘萬；

translations.literal: At the beginning of his tenure the river treasury held more than one hundred thousand taels of silver;
translations.idiomatic: When he took office the river treasury held more than one hundred thousand taels;

sentences.zh: 頻年撙節，現今貯庫四十六萬有奇。

translations.literal: Through years of economizing, the treasury now holds a little more than four hundred and sixty thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Years of thrift had left more than four hundred and sixty thousand taels in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 覈其官守，可謂公忠。

translations.literal: Examining his conduct in office, it may be called public-spirited and loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by his conduct in office, he had been scrupulously loyal.

sentences.zh: 及至積勞攖疾，以河事孔亟，不敢請告。

translations.literal: When accumulated labor brought on illness, because river affairs were urgently pressing he did not dare request leave.
translations.idiomatic: When overwork brought on illness, the river crisis was so urgent that he dared not ask for leave.

sentences.zh: 北往臨清，南至邳、宿，夙病日增，遂以不起。

translations.literal: He went north to Linqing and south to Pi and Su; his old illness grew daily worse, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled north to Linqing and south to Pi and Su; his chronic illness worsened daily, and he died.

sentences.zh: 年止四十有四，未有子嗣。

translations.literal: He was only forty-four years old and had no son to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was only forty-four and left no heir.

sentences.zh: 籥請恩卹，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: Yue requested favor and condolence payments, and funeral sacrifices and burial honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yue petitioned for posthumous honors, and state funeral rites were granted.

sentences.zh: 」徐、兗、淮、揚間頌之錫惠政，相傳死為河神。

translations.literal: Between Xu, Yan, Huai, and Yang they praised Zhixi’s benevolent administration, and it was handed down that after death he became a river god.
translations.idiomatic: Across Xu, Yan, Huai, and Yang people praised Zhixi’s benevolent rule, and legend held that after death he became a river god.

sentences.zh: 十二年，河道總督王光裕請錫封號，部議不行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the river director-general Wang Guangyu requested an ennobling title for Zhixi; the ministry deliberated and did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1673) river director Wang Guangyu asked that Zhixi receive an ennobling title; the ministry refused.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十五年，高宗南巡視河工，始允大學士阿桂等請，封助順永寧侯，春秋祠祭。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong, when the Gaozong made a southern tour to inspect river works, he at last approved the request of Grand Secretary Agui and others, enfeoffing him as Marquis Zhushun Yongning, with spring and autumn sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year of Qianlong (1780), on his southern tour to inspect river works, the Gaozong at last granted Grand Secretary Agui’s request and enfeoffed Zhixi as Marquis Who Assists Compliance and Brings Lasting Peace, with sacrifices each spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 嗣加號曰「佑安」，民稱之曰硃大王。

translations.literal: Later an additional title “You’an” was added, and the people called him Lord Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: A later title “Who Protects Peace” was added, and the people called him Lord Zhu.

sentences.zh: 崔維雅，字大醇，直隸大名人。

translations.literal: Cui Weiya, courtesy name Dachun, was a native of Daming in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Weiya, styled Dachun, was from Daming in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治三年舉人，授濬縣教諭，遷河南儀封知縣。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed instructor of Jun county and transferred to magistrate of Yifeng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the third year of Shunzhi (1646), became instructor of Jun county, and was transferred to magistrate of Yifeng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 儀封瀕河，歲苦氾濫，北岸三家莊當水沖，十四年，水勢北注，岸崩五里餘。

translations.literal: Yifeng bordered the river and suffered flooding every year; on the north bank Sanjiazhuang bore the brunt of the current; in the fourteenth year the water’s force poured north and the bank collapsed for more than five li.
translations.idiomatic: Yifeng lay on the river and flooded yearly; on the north bank Sanjiazhuang took the main current; in the fourteenth year (1657) the flood swung north and the bank gave way for more than five li.

sentences.zh: 維雅於上游故流疏使東行，北岸得安。

translations.literal: Weiya dredged the old channel upstream to make the river flow east, and the north bank was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Weiya dredged an old upstream channel to turn the river east, securing the north bank.

sentences.zh: 復與塞封丘大王廟決口，之錫疏薦，擢開封南河同知。

translations.literal: He also assisted in sealing the breach at Dawangmiao in Fengqiu; Zhixi memorialized recommending him, and he was promoted to sub-prefect of the South River at Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped seal the Fengqiu Dawangmiao breach; Zhixi recommended him and he was promoted South River sub-prefect at Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年五月，曹縣石香爐村河決，士民求速塞，維雅持不可。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Kangxi the river broke at Shixianglu Village in Cao county; gentry and commoners asked for rapid sealing, but Weiya held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Kangxi (1662) the river burst at Shixianglu in Cao county; locals demanded quick repair, but Weiya insisted it could not be rushed.

sentences.zh: 工將成復潰，至冬乃塞，如維雅言。

translations.literal: When the work was nearly done it collapsed again; only in winter was it sealed, just as Weiya had said.
translations.idiomatic: The work nearly finished, then collapsed again; sealing succeeded only in winter, as Weiya had predicted.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江寧波知府，光裕疏薦，擢河南河道副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Ningbo in Zhejiang; Guangyu memorialized recommending him, and he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Henan River Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Ningbo in Zhejiang; Guangyu recommended him and he was made Henan river vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時沿河千餘裡，險工迭出，維雅常預為之備，得無事。

translations.literal: At that time along more than a thousand li of river dangerous works arose in succession; Weiya often prepared for them in advance and kept matters untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Along more than a thousand li of river, dangerous works kept appearing; Weiya usually prepared in advance and kept disasters at bay.

sentences.zh: 陽武潭口寺堤直河衝，水勢迅急，下埽輒蟄。

translations.literal: The dike at Tankousi Temple in Yangwu faced the river head-on; the current was swift and mat-sinking below repeatedly failed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangwu Tankousi dike faced the main current head-on; the rush was fierce and mat revetments below kept sinking.

sentences.zh: 維雅預於上流疏引河，埽定，堤得固。

translations.literal: Weiya beforehand dredged and diverted the river upstream; the mats held firm and the dike was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Weiya dredged and diverted the river upstream in advance; the mats held and the dike stood firm.

sentences.zh: 虞城距河堤僅數里，堤沒入河，北岸引河沖刷不利。

translations.literal: Yucheng was only a few li from the river dike; the dike had been swallowed by the river, and diverting the current on the north bank was unfavorable for scouring.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng lay only a few li from the dike, which the river had swallowed; diverting the current on the north bank scoured poorly.

sentences.zh: 維雅預迎河溜挑濬，及秋水歸新河，舊河為平陸。

translations.literal: Weiya beforehand met the river’s rush with dredging; when autumn water returned to the new channel, the old river became level land.
translations.idiomatic: Weiya met the current with advance dredging; when autumn water entered the new channel, the old bed became dry land.

sentences.zh: 桃源七里溝河屢塞屢決，光裕檄維雅往勘，維雅言引河淺狹，流緩沙停，激盪無力，宜令河頭加寬闊，使足翕受全河；

translations.literal: The Qiligou River in Taoyuan repeatedly silted and repeatedly broke; Guangyu dispatched Weiya to survey it; Weiya said the diversion channel was shallow and narrow, the flow slow and sand settling, with no force to scour—the river mouth should be widened so it could fully receive the whole river;
translations.idiomatic: Taoyuan’s Qiligou River silted and burst repeatedly; Guangyu sent Weiya to survey it; Weiya said the diversion was shallow and narrow, the flow sluggish and sand settling, too weak to scour—the mouth should be widened to take the full river;

sentences.zh: 又待河水突漲，乃使開放，建瓴直下。

translations.literal: and one should wait until the river water suddenly rose, then open it so it would pour down like water from a elevated vessel.
translations.idiomatic: then wait for a sudden flood before opening it, so the current would pour down like water from a tilted jar.

sentences.zh: 又言下游數十里已成平陸，而引河僅百丈，節短勢蹙，力不能刷淤，當接挑二百丈闊，損十之八而深半之。

translations.literal: He also said that downstream for several tens of li had already become level land, while the diversion was only a hundred zhang—too short and cramped in force to scour silt; it should be extended by dredging two hundred zhang in width, reducing width by eight-tenths and depth by half.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that dozens of li downstream had become dry land while the diversion was only a hundred zhang—too short and cramped to scour silt; it should be extended two hundred zhang wide, narrowing width by four-fifths and halving depth.

sentences.zh: 又言開放當在河頭西北，留近埽五丈勿開，則河流入口有倒瀉之勢，埽亦迎流下。

translations.literal: He also said opening should be at the northwest of the river mouth, leaving five zhang near the revetment unopened, so the river’s entry would have a back-pouring force and the revetment would also meet the downward flow.
translations.idiomatic: Opening should be at the northwest of the mouth, leaving five zhang by the revetment closed so the entry would back-scour and the revetment meet the downward rush.

sentences.zh: 光裕悉用其議。

translations.literal: Guangyu adopted all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyu adopted all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 复遷河南按察使，湖南、廣西布政使，內召為大理寺卿。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Henan surveillance commissioner, then Hunan and Guangxi provincial administration commissioner, and summoned to the capital as president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He became Henan surveillance commissioner, then Hunan and Guangxi administration commissioner, and was summoned to the capital as president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 維雅治河主疏導引河，使水有所歸，故屢有功而後不為患。

translations.literal: Weiya’s river control emphasized dredging and diverting the river so that water had somewhere to go; therefore he often achieved success and later troubles did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Weiya’s river policy stressed dredging and diversion so water had an outlet; he often succeeded and left no lasting trouble.

sentences.zh: 當靳輔興大工時，維雅奏上所著河防芻議、兩河治略，並詆諆輔所行諸法，列二十四事難之。

translations.literal: When Jin Fu launched great works, Weiya memorialized submitting his River Defense Draft Discussions and General Plan for the Two Rivers, and also slandered the methods Fu was carrying out, listing twenty-four points of objection.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Fu launched his great river project, Weiya submitted his Draft Discussions on River Defense and General Plan for the Two Rivers, attacked Fu’s methods, and listed twenty-four objections.

sentences.zh: 輔疏辨，謂維雅說不可行，寢其議。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized in defense, saying Weiya’s proposals were impracticable, and his plan was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Fu rebutted that Weiya’s plan was unworkable, and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 靳輔，字紫垣，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Jin Fu, courtesy name Ziyuan, was a man of the Han Army Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu, styled Ziyuan, belonged to the Han Military Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，以官學生考授國史館編修，改內閣中書，遷兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, as a student of the Imperial Academy he passed examination and was appointed compiler of the State Historiography Office, then changed to secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and was transferred to vice director of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shunzhi (1652), as an Imperial Academy student he passed examination, became State Historiography compiler, then Grand Secretariat secretary, and rose to vice director of War.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，自郎中四遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, from director he was promoted four times to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi he rose through four promotions from director to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十年，授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1671) he was made governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 疏請行溝田法，以十畝為一鞬，二十鞬為一溝。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting implementation of the ditch-field method, with ten mu as one ridge unit and twenty ridge units as one ditch.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for the ditch-field system: ten mu per ridge unit, twenty ridge units per ditch.

sentences.zh: 溝土累為道，道高溝低，澇則洩水，旱以灌田。

translations.literal: Earth from the ditch was piled into ridges; ridges were high and ditches low—when flooded water drained off, in drought it irrigated the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Ditch spoil formed ridges higher than the ditches—draining floods in wet years and irrigating in drought.

sentences.zh: 會三籓亂起，不果行。

translations.literal: Just then the rebellion of the Three Feudatories broke out, and it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Feudatories rebellion broke out before it could be implemented.

sentences.zh: 部議裁驛站經費，輔疏請禁差員橫索、騷擾驛遞，歲終節存驛站、摃腳等項二十四萬有奇。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated on cutting post-station expenses; Fu memorialized requesting prohibition of traveling commissioners’ extortion and harassment of the courier system; by year’s end he saved more than two hundred and forty thousand taels on post stations, porter fees, and other items.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry proposed cutting post-station funds, Fu memorialized to stop traveling commissioners’ extortion and harassment of couriers; by year’s end he saved more than two hundred and forty thousand taels on stations, porter fees, and related costs.

sentences.zh: 上獎輔實心任事，加兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Fu for conscientious service and gave him the additional rank of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Fu’s conscientious service and gave him the concurrent rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授河道總督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Director-General of Rivers and Canals.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1677) he was made Director-General of Rivers and Canals.

sentences.zh: 時河道久不治，歸仁堤、王家營、邢家口、古溝、翟家壩等處先後潰溢，高家堰決三十餘處，淮水全入運河，黃水逆上至清水潭，浸淫四出。

translations.literal: At that time the river course had long gone untended; at Guiren Dike, Wangjiaying, Xingjiakou, Gugou, Zhaijiaba, and other places breaches and overflows occurred in succession; Gaojiayan broke in more than thirty places; Huai water entirely entered the Grand Canal; Yellow River water backed up to Qingshuitan and spread in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: The river had long gone untended; Guiren Dike, Wangjiaying, Xingjiakou, Gugou, Zhaijiaba, and other sites breached in turn; Gaojiayan failed in thirty places; the Huai poured wholly into the Grand Canal; Yellow River water backed up to Qingshuitan and spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 碭山以東兩岸決口數十處，下河七州縣淹為大澤，清口涸為陸地。

translations.literal: East of Dangshan on both banks were dozens of breach openings; the seven prefectures and counties of the lower river were inundated into a great marsh; Qingkou dried into dry land.
translations.idiomatic: East of Dangshan both banks had dozens of breaches; seven lower-river prefectures and counties became a vast lake; Qingkou dried to land.

sentences.zh: 輔到官，週度形勢，博採輿論，為八疏同日上之：首議疏下流，自清江浦至雲梯關，於河身兩旁離水三丈，各挑引河一道，俟黃、淮下注，新舊河合為一，即以所挑土築兩岸大堤，南始白洋河，北始清河縣，並東至雲梯關。

translations.literal: When Fu took office he surveyed the situation all around and widely gathered public opinion, submitting eight memorials on the same day: the first proposed dredging the lower reach from Qingjiangpu to Yuntiguan, three zhang from the water on both sides of the river channel each digging one diversion channel; when the Yellow and Huai descended, old and new rivers would unite into one, and with the excavated earth build great dikes on both banks, south from Baiyang River, north from Qinghe county, both extending east to Yuntiguan.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Fu surveyed the terrain and gathered opinion, submitting eight memorials the same day: first, dredge the lower reach from Qingjiangpu to Yuntiguan—dig one diversion channel three zhang from the water on each bank; when Yellow and Huai water descended, old and new channels would merge, and excavated earth would build great dikes from Baiyang River in the south and Qinghe county in the north east to Yuntiguan.

sentences.zh: 雲梯關至海口百里，近海二十里，潮大土濕，不能施工；

translations.literal: From Yuntiguan to the sea mouth was a hundred li; within twenty li of the sea the tides were great and the soil wet, and work could not be done;
translations.idiomatic: From Yuntiguan to the sea was a hundred li; within twenty li of the coast tides were strong and soil too wet for work;

sentences.zh: 餘八十里亦宜量加疏濬，築堤以束之，限二百日畢工，日用夫十二萬三千有奇。

translations.literal: the remaining eighty li should also be dredged as appropriate and dikes built to confine it, limited to two hundred days for completion, using more than one hundred and twenty-three thousand laborers daily.
translations.idiomatic: the remaining eighty li should be dredged and diked as needed, finished in two hundred days with more than one hundred twenty-three thousand workers daily.

sentences.zh: 次議治上流淤墊，洪澤湖下流自高家堰西至清口，為全淮會黃之所。

translations.literal: Next he proposed treating upstream silting: the lower reach of Hongze Lake from Gaojiayan west to Qingkou is where the whole Huai meets the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed treating upstream silt: Hongze Lake’s lower reach from Gaojiayan west to Qingkou is where the entire Huai meets the Yellow.

sentences.zh: 當於小河兩旁離水二十丈，各挑引河一道，分頭沖洗。

translations.literal: At the lesser river, twenty zhang from the water on both sides, each should dig one diversion channel to scour separately.
translations.idiomatic: At the lesser channel, twenty zhang from the water on each side, dig one diversion to scour separately.

sentences.zh: 次議培修七里墩、武家墩、高家墩、高良澗至周橋閘臨湖殘缺堤岸，下築坦坡，使水至平漫而上，順縮而下，不至怒激崩衝。

translations.literal: Next he proposed repairing and heightening the broken lakeside dikes from Qilidun, Wujiadun, Gaojiadun, and Gaoliangjian to Zhouqiao Sluice, building gentle slopes below so that when water arrived it would spread evenly upward and contract smoothly downward, not raging and bursting the banks.
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed repairing broken lakeside dikes from Qilidun, Wujiadun, Gaojiadun, and Gaoliangjian to Zhouqiao Sluice, building gentle slopes below so water would spread evenly and withdraw smoothly without violent erosion.

sentences.zh: 堤一尺、坦坡五尺，夯杵堅實，種草其上。

translations.literal: For each chi of dike, five chi of gentle slope, rammed solid with pestles, and grass planted on top.
translations.idiomatic: One chi of dike to five chi of slope, rammed solid and planted with grass.

sentences.zh: 次議塞黃、淮各處決口，例用埽，費鉅且不耐久；

translations.literal: Next he proposed sealing breaches of the Yellow and Huai at various places; the usual method used mat revetments, which were costly and not durable;
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed sealing Yellow and Huai breaches; the usual mat revetments were costly and short-lived;

sentences.zh: 求築土禦水之法，宜密下排椿，多加板纜，用蒲包裹土，麻繩縛而填之，費省而工固。

translations.literal: seeking a method of building earth to resist water: closely drive rows of piles, add many planks and cables, wrap earth in rush mats, bind with hemp rope and fill in—cost saving and work solid.
translations.idiomatic: he sought an earthen method: drive piles closely, add planks and cables, wrap earth in rush mats bound with hemp rope—cheaper and sturdier.

sentences.zh: 次議閉通濟閘壩，濬清口至清水潭運河二百三十里，以所挑之土傾東西兩堤之外，西隄築為坦坡，東堤加培堅厚，次議規畫經費，都計需銀二百十四萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: Next he proposed closing the Tongji Sluice dam, dredging the canal from Qingkou to Qingshuitan for two hundred and thirty li, dumping excavated earth outside the east and west dikes, building the west dike as a gentle slope and thickening the east dike; next he proposed planning expenses, totaling a little more than two million one hundred and forty-eight thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed closing the Tongji dam, dredging the two hundred thirty li from Qingkou to Qingshuitan, dumping spoil outside both dikes with a gentle slope on the west and a thickened east bank; total cost would exceed 2.148 million taels.

sentences.zh: 宜令直隸、江南、浙江、山東、江西、湖北各州縣預徵康熙二十年錢糧十之一，約二百萬。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties of Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Shandong, Jiangxi, and Hubei should be ordered to collect in advance one-tenth of the twentieth year of Kangxi land tax, about two million.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Shandong, Jiangxi, and Hubei should advance one-tenth of the Kangxi twentieth-year land tax—about two million taels.

sentences.zh: 工成後，令淮、揚被水田畝納三錢至一錢；

translations.literal: After the works were completed, flooded paddy fields in Huai and Yang should pay three qian to one qian per mu;
translations.idiomatic: After completion, flooded fields in Huai and Yang would pay three to one qian per mu;

sentences.zh: 運河經過，商貨米豆石納二分，他貨物斤四分；

translations.literal: along the canal route, merchants’ rice and beans would pay two fen per shi, other goods four fen per jin;
translations.idiomatic: along the canal, rice and beans would pay two fen per shi, other goods four fen per jin;

sentences.zh: 並開武生納監事例，如數補還。

translations.literal: and the precedent of military students purchasing supervision status would be opened to make up the amount.
translations.idiomatic: and military students could buy supervision status to make up the sum.

sentences.zh: 次議裁併冗員，明定職守，並嚴河工處分，諱決視諱盜；

translations.literal: Next he proposed cutting redundant posts, clarifying duties, and strictly punishing river works—treating concealment of breaches like concealment of banditry;
translations.idiomatic: Next he proposed cutting redundant posts, clarifying duties, and punishing river officials who concealed breaches as they would bandits;

sentences.zh: 兼請調用官吏，工成，與原屬河廳官吏並得優敘。

translations.literal: he also requested transfer of officials; when the works were completed, both transferred officials and original river-office officials would receive favorable evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to transfer officials; on completion both transferred men and original river-office staff would receive favorable evaluation.

sentences.zh: 次議工竣後，設河兵守堤，裡設兵六名至二名，都計五千八百六十名。

translations.literal: Next, after completion, establish river soldiers to guard dikes, from six to two soldiers per li, totaling five thousand eight hundred and sixty men.
translations.idiomatic: Finally, after completion, post river soldiers along the dikes—two to six per li, five thousand eight hundred sixty in all.

sentences.zh: 疏入，下廷議，以方軍興，复舉大工，役夫每日至十二萬餘，召募擾民，應先擇要修築。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it was sent for court deliberation; because military campaigns were underway and great works were again being launched, with more than one hundred and twenty thousand laborers daily and recruitment disturbing the people, the essential repairs should be chosen first.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to court; with war underway and more than one hundred twenty thousand daily laborers disturbing the people, the court ruled that essential repairs should come first.

sentences.zh: 上命輔熟籌。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Fu to plan carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fu to plan carefully.

sentences.zh: 十七年，輔疏言：「以驢運土，可減募夫之半；

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Fu memorialized, saying: “Using donkeys to transport earth can reduce hired laborers by half;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year (1678) Fu wrote: “Donkey transport of earth can halve hired labor;

sentences.zh: 初擬二百日畢工，今改為四百日，又可減募夫之半。

translations.literal: the initial plan was two hundred days to completion; now changed to four hundred days, laborers can again be reduced by half.”
translations.idiomatic: the original two-hundred-day schedule is now four hundred days, halving labor again.”

sentences.zh: 」河工故事，大堤謂之「遙堤」，堤內復為堤逼水，謂之「縷堤」，兩堤間為橫堤，謂之「格堤」。

translations.literal: In river-work precedent the great dike is called the “distant dike”; within the dike another dike is built to press the water, called the “continuous dike”; between the two dikes cross dikes are built, called the “check dike.”
translations.idiomatic: In river-work usage the main dike is the “distant dike”; an inner dike pressing the water is the “continuous dike”; cross dikes between them are “check dikes.”

sentences.zh: 輔疏請就原估土方加築縷堤，有餘量增格堤，南自白洋河，北自清河，上至徐州，視此興築。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized requesting that on the basis of the original estimated earthwork continuous dikes be added, and if there was surplus, check dikes increased, south from Baiyang River, north from Qinghe, up to Xuzhou, building according to this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu asked to add continuous dikes within the original earthwork estimate and check dikes where surplus allowed, from Baiyang River south and Qinghe north up to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 餘並如前議。

translations.literal: The rest followed the previous proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed his earlier plan.

sentences.zh: 疏入，復下廷議，允行。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, again sent for court deliberation, and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to court again and was approved.

sentences.zh: 上諭以治河大事，當動正項錢糧。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed that for the great matter of river control, regular budget funds should be used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that major river work must use regular budget funds.

sentences.zh: 輔疏言：「前議黃河兩岸分築遙、縷二隄，勘有舊堤貼近河身，擬作為縷堤，其外更築遙堤。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized, saying: “The previous proposal was to build distant and continuous dikes separately on both banks of the Yellow River; survey found old dikes close to the river channel, planned as continuous dikes, with distant dikes built outside them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu wrote: “The earlier plan was separate distant and continuous dikes on both Yellow River banks; survey found old dikes near the channel to serve as continuous dikes, with new distant dikes outside.

sentences.zh: 前議用驢運土，今議改車運。

translations.literal: The previous proposal used donkeys to transport earth; now it is proposed to change to cart transport.
translations.idiomatic: Donkey transport is now changed to cart transport.

sentences.zh: 前議離堤三十丈內不許取土，今因宿遷、桃源等縣人弱工多，改令二十丈外取土。

translations.literal: The previous proposal forbade taking earth within thirty zhang of the dike; now because in Suqian, Taoyuan, and other counties the people were weak and labor plentiful, it is changed to allow taking earth beyond twenty zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Earth could not be taken within thirty zhang of the dike; because Suqian, Taoyuan, and other counties had weak labor pools, earth may now be taken beyond twenty zhang.

sentences.zh: 前議河身兩旁各挑引河一道，今以工費浩繁，除清河北岸淺工必須挑濬。

translations.literal: The previous proposal was to dig one diversion channel on each side of the river channel; now because project costs are vast, except for shallow works on the north bank of the Qing River that must be dredged,
translations.idiomatic: Each bank was to get one diversion channel; costs are now too vast—only shallow north-bank Qing River work must be dredged.

sentences.zh: 餘俱用鐵掃帚濬深河底。

translations.literal: the rest will all use iron harrows to deepen the river bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere iron harrows will deepen the riverbed.”

sentences.zh: 」下部議，從之。

translations.literal: It was sent to the ministries for deliberation and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved.

sentences.zh: 是歲吳三桂死，上趣諸將帥進兵，輔欲節帑佐軍，又以興工後需費溢出原估，均頗改前議，先開清口引河四道，塞高家堰、王家岡、武家墩諸決口，築堤束水。

translations.literal: That year Wu Sangui died; the emperor urged the generals to advance; Fu wished to economize funds to assist the army, and because after launching works needed expenses exceeded the original estimate, he considerably altered previous proposals, first opening four diversion channels at Qingkou, sealing breaches at Gaojiayan, Wangjiagang, Wujiadun, and other places, and building dikes to confine the water.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wu Sangui died and the emperor pressed the generals forward; Fu sought to save funds for the army and, as costs exceeded estimates, revised his plan—first opening four Qingkou diversion channels, sealing Gaojiayan, Wangjiagang, Wujiadun, and other breaches, and building dikes to confine the water.

sentences.zh: 如所議施行。

translations.literal: It was carried out as deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Work proceeded as approved.

sentences.zh: 顧下流未大治，伏秋盛漲，水溢出堤上，復決碭山石將軍廟、蕭縣九里溝。

translations.literal: But the lower reach had not been greatly treated; at the height of the summer-autumn flood the water overflowed the dikes and again broke at Shijiangjun Temple in Dangshan and Jiuligou in Xiao county.
translations.idiomatic: But the lower reach was still untamed; at the summer-autumn flood peak water topped the dikes and broke again at Dangshan’s Shijiangjun Temple and Xiao county’s Jiuligou.

sentences.zh: 輔乃議設減水壩，於蕭、碭、宿遷、桃源、清河諸縣河南北兩岸為壩十三，壩七洞，水盛藉以宣洩。

translations.literal: Fu then proposed establishing flood-relief dams: on both banks south and north of the river in Xiao, Dang, Suqian, Taoyuan, Qinghe, and other counties, thirteen dams with seven openings, so that when water was abundant it could be released.
translations.idiomatic: Fu then proposed thirteen flood-relief dams with seven openings on both banks in Xiao, Dang, Suqian, Taoyuan, Qinghe, and other counties to discharge excess water.

sentences.zh: 輔复察清口淮、黃交會，黃漲侵灌運河，乃自新莊閘西南開新河至太平壩；

translations.literal: Fu again inspected the meeting of Huai and Yellow at Qingkou; the Yellow rose and inundated the Grand Canal; he therefore opened a new river southwest from Xinzhuang Sluice to Taiping Dam;
translations.idiomatic: Fu found that at Qingkou rising Yellow water was backing into the canal; he cut a new channel southwest from Xinzhuang Sluice to Taiping Dam;

sentences.zh: 又自文華寺開新河至七里閘，复折向西南，亦至太平壩；

translations.literal: and also opened a new river from Wenhua Temple to Qili Sluice, then turning southwest again to Taiping Dam;
translations.idiomatic: and another from Wenhua Temple to Qili Sluice, then southwest again to Taiping Dam;

sentences.zh: 改以七里閘為運口，由武家墩爛泥淺轉入黃河。

translations.literal: changing to use Qili Sluice as the transport mouth, turning through Wujiadun Lannini Shoal into the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: making Qili Sluice the transport mouth and routing grain traffic through Wujiadun’s Lannini Shoal into the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 運口距黃、淮交會處約十里，自此無淤墊之患。

translations.literal: The transport mouth was about ten li from where the Yellow and Huai met; from this there was no trouble of silting.
translations.idiomatic: The transport mouth lay about ten li from the Yellow-Huai junction, ending silting problems.

sentences.zh: 疏報，並議行。

translations.literal: He memorialized reporting this, and it was approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He reported by memorial and the plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 輔勘清水潭決口屢塞屢衝，乃棄深就淺，築東西長堤二道，並挑新河八百四十丈，疏積水。

translations.literal: Fu surveyed the Qingshuitan breach, which was repeatedly sealed and repeatedly breached; he abandoned the deep course for the shallow, built two long dikes east and west, and dug a new river eight hundred and forty zhang to drain accumulated water.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingshuitan, where breaches were sealed and reopened repeatedly, Fu abandoned the deep channel for a shallow one, built east and west long dikes, and cut an eight-hundred-forty-zhang new river to drain standing water.

sentences.zh: 山陽、高郵等七州縣民田，至是皆出水可耕。

translations.literal: The civilian fields of the seven prefectures and counties of Shanyang, Gaoyou, and others all emerged from water and could be cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Farmland in Shanyang, Gaoyou, and five other prefectures and counties emerged and could be planted again.

sentences.zh: 十八年，輔疏報，並請名新河曰永安河，報聞。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Fu memorialized reporting this and also requested that the new river be named Yong’an River; acknowledgment was received.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1679) Fu reported and asked that the new channel be named the Yong’an River; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 翟家壩淮河決口成支河九道，輔飭淮揚道副使劉國靖等督堵塞，至是工竟，輔詣勘疏報，並言：「山陽、寶應、高郵、江都四州縣瀦水諸湖，逐漸涸出。

translations.literal: At Zhaijiaba the Huai River breach had formed nine branch channels; Fu ordered Huai-Yang circuit vice commissioner Liu Guojing and others to supervise sealing; when the works were completed Fu went to survey and memorialized reporting, also saying: “The lakes holding water in the four prefectures and counties of Shanyang, Baoying, Gaoyou, and Jiangdu are gradually drying out.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhaijiaba the Huai breach had formed nine branch channels; Fu ordered Huai-Yang vice commissioner Liu Guojing and others to plug them; when the work was done Fu inspected and reported: “The flooded lakes of Shanyang, Baoying, Gaoyou, and Jiangdu are gradually drying.

sentences.zh: 臣今廣為招墾，俾增賦足民，上下均利。

translations.literal: Your servant now broadly invites reclamation, so that tax revenue may increase, the people be provided for, and both court and commoners alike benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I now propose broad reclamation so revenue may rise, the people be provided for, and court and subjects alike benefit.”

sentences.zh: 」屯田之議自此起。

translations.literal: The proposal for military colonies began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal for military colonies dates from this.

sentences.zh: 漕船自七里閘出口，行駱馬湖達窯灣。

translations.literal: Grain transport boats left through Qili Sluice, traveled Luoma Lake to reach Yaowan.
translations.idiomatic: Grain boats left through Qili Sluice, crossed Luoma Lake, and reached Yaowan.

sentences.zh: 夏秋盛漲，冬春水涸，重運多阻。

translations.literal: In summer and autumn floods were heavy; in winter and spring water dried up, and heavy transport was often blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Summer-autumn floods and winter-spring low water often blocked heavy transport.

sentences.zh: 輔議濬湖旁皁河故道，上接泇河通運。

translations.literal: Fu proposed dredging the old course of the Zao River beside the lake, connecting upward with the Si River to open transport.
translations.idiomatic: Fu proposed dredging the old Zao River course beside the lake to link the Si River with the transport route.

sentences.zh: 疏入，下廷議，上問諸臣意若何，左都御史魏象樞曰：「輔請大修黃河，上發帑二百五十一萬，計一勞永逸。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it was sent for court deliberation; the emperor asked what the ministers thought; the left censor-in-chief Wei Xiangshu said: “Fu requested great repairs on the Yellow River; the emperor disbursed two million five hundred and ten thousand from the treasury, planning that one effort would bring lasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to court; the emperor asked the ministers’ views; left censor-in-chief Wei Xiangshu said: “Fu asked for major Yellow River repairs; the emperor allocated 2.51 million taels for a permanent solution.

sentences.zh: 前奏堤壩已築十之七，今又欲別開河道，所謂一勞永逸者安在？

translations.literal: He previously reported that dikes and dams were seven-tenths built; now he again wishes to open a separate river channel—where is this so-called one effort for lasting ease?
translations.idiomatic: He reported dikes and dams seven-tenths complete; now he wants another new channel—where is the permanent solution?

sentences.zh: 臣等慮漕運有阻，故議從其請。

translations.literal: We ministers feared obstruction of grain transport, and therefore deliberated to approve his request.
translations.idiomatic: We feared for grain transport and so approved his request.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「象樞言良是。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Xiangshu speaks well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “Xiangshu is right.

sentences.zh: 河雖開，必上流浩瀚，方免淤滯。

translations.literal: Even if the river is opened, the upper reach must be vast and full before silting and stagnation can be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Even with a new channel open, the upper reach must run full and wide to avoid silting.

sentences.zh: 今雨少水涸，恐未必有濟。

translations.literal: Now rain is scant and the water has dried up; I fear it may not necessarily succeed.
translations.idiomatic: With so little rain and the water so low, I doubt it will help.

sentences.zh: 即已成諸工，亦以旱易修，豈得恃為永固耶？

translations.literal: Even if all the works are already completed, they are easy to repair in drought—how can one rely on them as permanently secure?
translations.idiomatic: Even finished works are easy to maintain in a drought—how can we treat them as permanently secure?

sentences.zh: 」十九年五月，輔丁憂，命在任守制。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the nineteenth year, Fu entered mourning for his father; he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year nineteen (1680), Fu went into mourning for his father but was ordered to remain in office while observing filial rites.

sentences.zh: 秋，河復決，輔疏請處分，上趣輔修築。

translations.literal: In autumn the river broke again; Fu memorialized requesting punishment; the emperor urged Fu to repair and build.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the river breached again; Fu submitted a memorial asking to be punished, but the emperor ordered him to press on with repairs.

sentences.zh: 二十年三月，輔疏言：「臣前請大修黃河，限三年水歸故道。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year, Fu memorialized: "Your subject previously requested a great repair of the Yellow River, with a limit of three years for the water to return to the old course.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year twenty (1681), Fu wrote: "Your subject had pledged a major Yellow River repair with the water back in the old channel within three years.

sentences.zh: 今限滿，水未歸故道，請處分。

translations.literal: Now the time limit has expired and the water has not returned to the old course; I request punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The term has expired and the water has not returned; I request punishment.

sentences.zh: 」下部議，當奪官，上命戴罪督修。

translations.literal: " It was sent to the ministries for deliberation; they held that his office should be stripped; the emperor ordered him to supervise repairs while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries recommended stripping his rank; the emperor ordered him to continue supervising repairs while bearing guilt.

sentences.zh: 二十一年五月，上遣尚書伊桑阿、侍郎宋文運、給事中王曰溫、御史伊喇喀勘工。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-first year, the emperor sent Ministers Yisang'a, Vice Minister Song Wenyun, Secretariat Secretary Wang Riwan, and Censor Yilake to inspect the works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year twenty-one (1682), the emperor dispatched Ministers Yisang'a and Song Wenyun, Secretariat Secretary Wang Riwan, and Censor Yilake to inspect the works.

sentences.zh: 候補布政使崔維雅奏上所著書，議盡罷輔所行減水壩諸法，大興工，日役夫四十萬，築堤以十二丈為率。

translations.literal: Acting Provincial Administration Commissioner Cui Weiya submitted the book he had written, proposing to abolish entirely the flood-relief dams and related methods Fu had implemented, launch great works employing four hundred thousand laborers a day, and build dikes at a standard height of twelve zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Provincial Commissioner Cui Weiya submitted his treatise, urging that Fu's flood-relief dams and related methods be scrapped entirely, that massive works employ four hundred thousand men a day, and that dikes be built to a standard height of twelve zhang.

sentences.zh: 上命從伊桑阿等往與輔議之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them to go with Yisang'a and the others to deliberate with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them to travel with Yisang'a's party and confer with Fu.

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿等遍勘諸工，至徐州，令輔與維雅議，輔疏言：「河道全局已成十八九。

translations.literal: Yisang'a and the others inspected all the works throughout; reaching Xuzhou, they ordered Fu to deliberate with Weiya. Fu memorialized: "The overall river situation is already eight or nine tenths complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yisang'a's party inspected the works up and down the line; at Xuzhou they had Fu meet with Weiya. Fu wrote: "The river system as a whole is already eight or nine tenths complete.

sentences.zh: 蕭家渡雖有決口，而海口大辟，下流疏通，腹心之害已除。

translations.literal: Though Xiaojiadu has a breach, the estuary has been greatly opened and the lower reach cleared—the mortal danger at the heart has been removed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojiadu still has a breach, but the estuary has been widened and the lower reach cleared—the core danger is gone.

sentences.zh: 斷不宜有所更張，隳成功，釀後患。

translations.literal: It is absolutely inadvisable to make changes, destroy what has succeeded, and breed later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: We must not change course now, wreck what has been achieved, and invite new disasters.

sentences.zh: 」伊桑阿等還京師，下廷議，工部尚書薩穆哈等請以蕭家渡決口責輔賠修，上以賠修非輔所能任，未允；

translations.literal: " When Yisang'a and the others returned to the capital, the matter was sent to court debate; Minister of Works Samuha and others asked that Fu be held liable to pay for repairs at the Xiaojiadu breach; the emperor held that compensation was beyond what Fu could bear and did not approve;
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, the case went to court. Minister of Works Samuha and others wanted Fu to pay for repairing the Xiaojiadu breach; the emperor held that compensation was beyond Fu's means and did not approve;

sentences.zh: 又議維雅條奏，伊桑阿請召輔詢之。

translations.literal: they also debated Cui Weiya's detailed memorial; Yisang'a asked to summon Fu for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: they also debated Cui Weiya's detailed proposals; Yisang'a asked that Fu be summoned for questioning.

sentences.zh: 十一月，輔入對，言蕭家渡工來歲正月當竟，維雅所議日用夫四十萬、築堤以十二丈為率，皆不可行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Fu appeared in audience and said the Xiaojiadu work would be finished by the first month of the coming year; Weiya's proposals of four hundred thousand laborers a day and dikes built to twelve zhang as the standard were all infeasible.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Fu appeared before the throne and said Xiaojiadu would be closed by the first month of the coming year; Weiya's plan for four hundred thousand men a day and twelve-zhang dikes was unworkable on every count.

sentences.zh: 維雅議乃寢。

translations.literal: Cui Weiya's proposals were then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Weiya's plan was set aside.

sentences.zh: 上命塞決口，仍動正項錢糧。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the breach sealed and still drew on regular budget funds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the breach plugged and authorized regular appropriations.

sentences.zh: 二十二年四月，輔疏報蕭家渡合龍，河歸故道，大溜直下，七里溝等四十餘處險汛日加，並天妃壩、王公堤及運河閘座，均應修築。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-second year, Fu memorialized reporting that Xiaojiadu had been closed, the river had returned to the old course, and the main current rushed straight down; more than forty dangerous reaches such as Qiligou grew worse day by day; Tianfei Dam, Wanggong Dike, and Grand Canal sluices all required repair.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year twenty-two (1683), Fu reported that Xiaojiadu was closed, the river was back in its old channel, and the main current ran straight; more than forty dangerous points such as Qiligou were worsening daily; Tianfei Dam, Wanggong Dike, and canal sluices all needed work.

sentences.zh: 別疏請飭河南巡撫修築開封、歸德兩府境河堤，防上流疏失。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he asked that the Henan governor be ordered to repair river dikes within the jurisdictions of Kaifeng and Guide prefectures, to guard against neglect on the upper reach.
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he urged the Henan governor to repair dikes in Kaifeng and Guide, lest the upper reach be left unattended.

sentences.zh: 上均如所請。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every request.

sentences.zh: 十二月，命复輔官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he ordered Fu's office restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fu's rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十月，上南巡，閱河北岸諸工，諭輔曰：「蕭家渡堤壩當培薄增卑，隨時修築。
