translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-third year, on his southern tour the emperor inspected works on the north bank of the river and instructed Fu: "The Xiaojiadu dikes and dams should be thickened where thin and raised where low, and repaired as needed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year twenty-three (1684), on his southern tour the emperor inspected the north-bank works and told Fu: "At Xiaojiadu, thicken what is thin, raise what is low, and keep the dikes in repair.

sentences.zh: 減水壩原用以洩水，遇泛溢橫流，安知今日減水壩不為他年之決口？

translations.literal: Flood-relief dams were originally for releasing water; when floods overflow and spread sideways, who knows whether today's relief dams will not become breaches in years to come?
translations.idiomatic: Relief dams were meant to spill excess water—but in a great flood water runs everywhere; who can say today's relief dam will not be tomorrow's breach?

sentences.zh: 且減水旁流，浸灌民田，朕心深不忍。

translations.literal: Moreover, the side flows from relief dams inundate the people's fields—my heart cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: And when relief water spreads into the fields, my heart cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 當籌畫措置。

translations.literal: You must plan and arrange measures.
translations.idiomatic: Find a remedy.

sentences.zh: 」上見堤夫作苦，駐轡慰勞久之，諭輔戒官役侵蝕工食。

translations.literal: The emperor saw the dike workers' toil, halted his carriage a long while to comfort them, and admonished Fu to warn officials and clerks against embezzling workers' rations.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the laborers' hardship, he halted his carriage a long while to comfort them and warned Fu to stop officials from skimming workers' rations.

sentences.zh: 復視天妃閘，諭輔宜改草壩，並另設七里、太平二閘殺水勢。

translations.literal: He again inspected Tianfei Sluice and instructed Fu to replace the earthen dam and additionally establish the Qili and Taiping sluices to reduce the force of the water.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected Tianfei Sluice again and told Fu to replace the earthen dam and add Qili and Taiping sluices to tame the current.

sentences.zh: 舟過高郵，見田廬在水中，惻然愍念。

translations.literal: When the boat passed Gaoyou and he saw fields and houses in the water, he was deeply moved with compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Gaoyou he saw farms and homes awash and was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書伊桑阿、薩穆哈察視海口。

translations.literal: He sent Ministers Yisang'a and Samuha to inspect the estuary.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ministers Yisang'a and Samuha to survey the sea mouth.

sentences.zh: 還蹕，复閱高家堰，至清口，閱黃河南岸諸工，諭輔運口當添建閘座，防黃水倒灌；

translations.literal: On the return journey he again inspected Gaojiayan; reaching Qingkou, he inspected works on the south bank of the Yellow River and instructed Fu that sluices should be added at the transport mouth to guard against Yellow water backing in;
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey he revisited Gaojiayan and Qingkou, inspected the south-bank Yellow River works, and told Fu to add sluices at the transport mouth against Yellow backflow;

sentences.zh: 復召輔入行宮慰諭，書閱河堤詩賜之。

translations.literal: he again summoned Fu to the traveling palace to console him and bestowed a poem on inspecting river dikes.
translations.idiomatic: he summoned Fu again to the traveling palace to encourage him and presented a poem composed on inspecting the river dikes.

sentences.zh: 輔以上念減水淹民，因議於宿遷、桃源、清河三縣黃河北岸堤內開新河，謂之中河。

translations.literal: Because the emperor was concerned that relief dams were flooding the people, Fu proposed opening a new river inside the north-bank dikes of Suqian, Taoyuan, and Qinghe counties on the Yellow River—called the Middle River.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the emperor's concern that relief dams were drowning farmland, Fu proposed cutting a new channel inside the north-bank dikes of Suqian, Taoyuan, and Qinghe—the "Middle River."

sentences.zh: 於清河西仲家莊建閘，引攔馬河減水壩所洩水入中河。

translations.literal: At Zhongjiazhuang west of the Qing River he built a sluice to draw water discharged from the Luoma River relief dams into the Middle River.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongjiazhuang, west of the Qing River, he built a sluice to take spill from the Luoma River relief dams into the Middle River.

sentences.zh: 漕船初出清口浮於河，至張莊運口，中河成，得自清口截流，迳渡北岸，度仲家莊閘，免黃河一百八十里之險。

translations.literal: Grain boats at first floated on the river after leaving Qingkou as far as the Zhangzhuang transport mouth; once the Middle River was complete, they could cut across from Qingkou to the north bank, pass Zhongjiazhuang Sluice, and avoid one hundred eighty li of danger on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Grain boats had first to float downriver from Qingkou to Zhangzhuang; once the Middle River was open they could cross from Qingkou to the north bank, pass Zhongjiazhuang Sluice, and skip one hundred eighty li of Yellow River peril.

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿等還奏，議疏濬車路、串場諸河至白駒、丁溪、草堰諸口，引高郵等處減水壩所洩水入海。

translations.literal: When Yisang'a and the others returned and reported, they proposed dredging the Chelu, Chuan'chang, and related rivers to the Baixu, Dingxi, and Caoyan outlets, drawing water discharged from relief dams at Gaoyou and elsewhere out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Yisang'a's party returned and proposed dredging Chelu, Chuan'chang, and related channels to Baixu, Dingxi, and Caoyan, carrying spill from Gaoyou and other relief dams to the sea.

sentences.zh: 上命安徽按察使於成龍董其事，仍受輔節制，奏事由輔疏報。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Anhui Provincial Judge Yu Chenglong to direct the work, still under Fu's command; memorials were to be submitted through Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor put Anhui Provincial Judge Yu Chenglong in charge, still under Fu's authority, with reports routed through Fu.

sentences.zh: 二十四年正月，輔疏請徐州迤上毛城鋪、王家山諸處增建減水閘，下廷議。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year, Fu memorialized requesting additional relief sluices at Maochengpu, Wangjiashan, and other places above Xuzhou; the matter was sent to court debate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year twenty-four (1685), Fu asked to add relief sluices at Maochengpu, Wangjiashan, and other sites above Xuzhou; the proposal went to court.

sentences.zh: 上諭減水閘益河工無益百姓，不可不熟計，命遣官與輔詳議，若分水不致多損民田，即令興工。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed that relief sluices benefit river works but not the common people and must not be adopted without careful calculation; he ordered officials sent to deliberate in detail with Fu, and if diverting water would not greatly harm the people's fields, work might proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said relief sluices help the river, not the people, and must be weighed carefully; officials were sent to confer with Fu—if diversion would not ruin too much farmland, work could begin.

sentences.zh: 九月，輔疏報赴河南勘黃河兩岸，請築考城、儀封、封丘、滎澤堤埽，下部議行。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Fu memorialized reporting that he had gone to Henan to survey both banks of the Yellow River and requested dikes and revetments at Kaocheng, Yifeng, Fengqiu, and Yingze; the ministries deliberated and approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fu reported a survey of both Henan banks and asked for dikes at Kaocheng, Yifeng, Fengqiu, and Yingze; the ministries approved.

sentences.zh: 成龍議疏海口洩積水，輔謂下河地卑於海五尺，疏海口引潮內侵，害滋大；

translations.literal: Chenglong proposed dredging the estuary to drain accumulated water; Fu said the lower-river region was five chi lower than the sea and that dredging the estuary would draw the tide inland—the harm would be greater;
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong wanted the sea mouth dredged to drain standing water; Fu argued the lower river lies five chi below sea level and dredging would pull the tide inland and make things worse;

sentences.zh: 議自高郵東車邏鎮築堤，歷興化白駒場，束所洩水入海，堤內涸出田畝，丈量還民，餘招民屯墾，取田價償工費。

translations.literal: he proposed building a dike east from Cheluo town in Gaoyou through Xinghua's Baixu field to confine discharged water and send it to sea; fields dried out inside the dike would be measured and returned to the people, and the remainder would be opened to colonization, with land prices taken to repay project costs.
translations.idiomatic: he proposed a dike east from Gaoyou's Cheluo town through Xinghua's Baixu salt field to the sea to pen the spill; reclaimed land inside would be surveyed and returned to owners, the rest colonized, with land sales covering costs.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，上謂取田價恐累民，未即許。

translations.literal: When the memorial was received, the emperor said that taking land prices might burden the people and did not immediately approve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared charging for reclaimed land would burden the people and withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 尋召輔、成龍馳驛詣京師廷議，成龍議開海口故道，輔仍主築長堤高一丈五尺，束水敵海潮。

translations.literal: Soon Fu and Chenglong were summoned post-haste to the capital for court debate; Chenglong argued for opening the old estuary channel, while Fu still advocated building a long dike one zhang and five chi high to confine the water against the sea tide.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Chenglong were soon rushed to Beijing for a court debate: Chenglong for reopening the old sea mouth, Fu for a long dike one zhang five chi high to hold the water against the tide.

sentences.zh: 大學士、九卿從輔議，通政使參議成其範、給事中王又旦、御史錢鎯從成龍議，議不決。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretaries and Nine Ministers sided with Fu; Privy Councilor Cheng Qifan, Secretariat Secretary Wang Youdan, and Censor Qian Peng sided with Chenglong; no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries and the Nine Ministers backed Fu; Privy Councilor Cheng Qifan, Secretariat Secretary Wang Youdan, and Censor Qian Peng backed Chenglong; the court could not decide.

sentences.zh: 上命宣問下河諸州縣人官京師者，侍讀寶應喬萊等乃言：「從成龍議，工易成，百姓有利無害；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered officials from the lower-river prefectures and counties serving in the capital to be questioned; Reader from Bao'an Qiao Lai and others then said: "Following Chenglong's plan, the work is easy to complete and the common people benefit without harm;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned lower-river officials in the capital; Reader Qiao Lai of Bao'an and others said: "Chenglong's plan is easier to finish and helps the people without harm;

sentences.zh: 從輔議，工難成，百姓田廬墳墓多傷損，且堤高一丈五尺，束水至一丈，高於民居，伏秋潰決，為害不可勝言。

translations.literal: following Fu's plan, the work is hard to complete, and the people's fields, houses, and graves suffer much damage; moreover, with a dike one zhang and five chi high confining water to a depth of one zhang, higher than dwellings, a breach in the summer-autumn flood season would bring harm beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's plan is hard to finish and will wreck fields, homes, and graves; a dike one zhang five chi high holding a foot of water above the houses would, if it burst in flood season, bring disaster beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 」上頗右成龍，遣尚書薩穆哈、學士穆稱額詣淮安會漕督徐旭齡、巡撫湯斌詳勘。

translations.literal: " The emperor somewhat favored Chenglong and sent Minister Samuha and Academician Much'a'e to Huai'an to join Grain Transport Director Xu Xuling and Governor Tang Bin for a detailed survey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaned toward Chenglong and sent Samuha and Academician Much'a'e to Huai'an with Grain Transport Director Xu Xuling and Governor Tang Bin for a full survey.

sentences.zh: 二十五年正月，薩穆哈等還奏，謂民間皆言濬海口無益。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fifth year, when Samuha and the others returned and reported, they said the people all declared that dredging the estuary was useless.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year twenty-five (1686), Samuha's party returned reporting that common opinion held estuary dredging useless.

sentences.zh: 尋授成龍直隸巡撫，罷濬海口議。

translations.literal: Soon Chenglong was appointed governor of Zhili, and the estuary-dredging proposal was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong was soon made Zhili governor and the estuary dredging plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 四月，召斌為尚書，入對，上复舉其事以問，斌言濬海口必有益於民。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Tang Bin was summoned as minister; in audience the emperor again raised the matter and asked; Bin said dredging the estuary would certainly benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Tang Bin was summoned to court as minister; asked again, he insisted estuary dredging would help the people.

sentences.zh: 上責薩穆哈、穆稱額還京時不以實奏，奪官。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Samuha and Much'a'e for not reporting truthfully when they returned to the capital and stripped their offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Samuha and Much'a'e for false reporting on their return and stripped their ranks.

sentences.zh: 召大學士九卿及萊等定議濬海口，發帑二十萬，命侍郎孫在豐董其役。

translations.literal: He summoned the Grand Secretaries, Nine Ministers, and Lai and others to decide on dredging the estuary, disbursed two hundred thousand taels from the treasury, and ordered Vice Minister Sun Zaifeng to direct the labor.
translations.idiomatic: He convened the Grand Secretaries, Nine Ministers, and Lai's group, approved estuary dredging, allocated two hundred thousand taels, and put Vice Minister Sun Zaifeng in charge.

sentences.zh: 工部劾輔治河已九年，無成功。

translations.literal: The Board of Works impeached Fu for nine years of river work without success.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Works impeached Fu: nine years on the river without success.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「河務甚難，而輔易視之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "River affairs are very difficult, yet Fu treats them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "River work is desperately hard, yet Fu has treated it lightly.

sentences.zh: 若遽議處，後任者益難為力，今姑寬之，仍責令督修。

translations.literal: If punishment is deliberated hastily, those who succeed him will find it even harder to act; for now let him be leniently dealt with and still charged to supervise repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Punish him now and his successor will have it harder still; for the moment I will be lenient and still hold him to the work.

sentences.zh: 」二十六年，輔疏言：「運堤減水以下河為壑，東即大海，濬海口似可紓水患；

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Fu memorialized: "Relief water from the transport dikes takes the lower river as its basin; to the east lies the sea; dredging the estuary seems able to ease flood trouble;
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six (1687), Fu wrote: "Relief from the transport dikes pours into the lower river basin; east lies the sea—dredging the mouth seems to offer relief;

sentences.zh: 惟泰州安豐、東台、鹽城諸縣地勢甚卑，形如釜底，若止就此挑濬，徒增其深。

translations.literal: only the terrain of Anfeng, Dongtai, Yancheng, and other counties in Taizhou is very low, shaped like the bottom of a cauldron; if dredging is done only there, it merely deepens the depression.
translations.idiomatic: but Anfeng, Dongtai, Yancheng, and other Taizhou counties lie in a bowl—dredge only there and you only dig the bowl deeper.

sentences.zh: ​​淮流甚漲，高家堰洩水洶湧而來，仍不能救民田之淹沒。

translations.literal: The Huai current swells greatly; water discharged from Gaojiayan rushes in torrents—and still cannot save the people's fields from inundation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai runs high, Gaojiayan spill thunders in—and still the fields drown.

sentences.zh: 臣以為杜患於流，不若杜患於源。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that stopping harm in the flow is not as good as stopping harm at the source.
translations.idiomatic: Better to stop the harm at its source than downstream.

sentences.zh: 高家堰堤外直東為下河，東北為清口，當自翟家壩起至高家堰築重堤萬六千丈，束減水北出清口，則洪澤湖不復東淹下河。

translations.literal: Straight east outside the Gaojiayan dike is the lower river; northeast is Qingkou; from Zhaijiaba to Gaojiayan a heavy dike sixteen thousand zhang long should be built to confine relief water and send it north out through Qingkou—then Hongze Lake will no longer flood the lower river to the east.
translations.idiomatic: East of Gaojiayan lies the lower river; northeast lies Qingkou—from Zhaijiaba to Gaojiayan build sixteen thousand zhang of heavy dike to pen relief water and send it north through Qingkou, and Hongze Lake will cease to flood the lower river eastward.

sentences.zh: 下河十餘萬頃皆成沃產，而高、寶諸湖涸出田畝，可招民屯墾，以裕河庫。

translations.literal: More than one hundred thousand mou of the lower river would all become fertile land, and fields dried out in the Gaoyou, Bao'an, and other lakes could be opened to colonization to enrich the river treasury.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand mou of lower river would turn fertile; lake beds at Gaoyou, Bao'an, and elsewhere could be colonized to fill the river treasury.

sentences.zh: 」上使以輔疏示成龍，成龍仍言下河宜開，重堤不宜築。

translations.literal: " The emperor had Fu's memorial shown to Chenglong; Chenglong still said the lower river should be opened and a heavy dike should not be built.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed Fu's memorial to Chenglong; Chenglong still insisted the lower river must be opened and opposed the heavy dike.

sentences.zh: 上遣尚書佛倫，侍郎熊一瀟，給事中達奇納、趙吉士與總督董訥，總漕慕天顏會勘。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Ministers Folun and Vice Minister Xiong Yixiao, Secretariat Secretaries Daqina and Zhao Jishi, together with Governor Dong Ne and Grain Transport Director Mu Tianyan, to conduct a joint survey.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister Folun, Vice Minister Xiong Yixiao, Secretaries Daqina and Zhao Jishi, Governor Dong Ne, and Transport Director Mu Tianyan to survey together.

sentences.zh: 佛倫等皆欲用輔議，天顏、在豐與相左。

translations.literal: Folun and the others all wished to adopt Fu's plan; Tianyan and Zaifeng opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: Folun's party favored Fu; Tianyan and Zaifeng dissented.

sentences.zh: 佛倫等還奏，下廷議，會太皇太后崩，議未上。

translations.literal: When Folun and the others returned and reported, the matter was sent to court debate; the Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang died, and the memorial was not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Folun returned and the case went to court—but the Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang died and the memorial never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十七年春，給事中劉楷，御史郭琇、陸祖修交章論輔，琇辭連輔幕客陳潢，祖修請罷輔，至以舜殛鯀為比；

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year, Secretariat Secretary Liu Kai and Censors Guo Xiu and Lu Zuxiu submitted successive memorials attacking Fu; Xiu's language implicated Fu's staff adviser Chen Huang; Zuxiu asked that Fu be dismissed, even comparing the case to Shun's execution of Gun;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year twenty-seven (1688), Secretariat Secretary Liu Kai and Censors Guo Xiu and Lu Zuxiu attacked Fu in turn; Xiu implicated his adviser Chen Huang; Zuxiu demanded dismissal, likening Fu to Gun punished by Shun;

sentences.zh: 天顏、在豐亦疏論屯田累民，及輔阻撓開濬下河狀。

translations.literal: Tianyan and Zaifeng also memorialized on how colonization burdened the people and on Fu's obstruction of dredging the lower river.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyan and Zaifeng added memorials on colonization harming the people and Fu blocking lower-river dredging.

sentences.zh: 琇旋劾大學士明珠等，語复及輔。

translations.literal: Xiu soon impeached Grand Secretary Mingzhu and others; his language again touched on Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu soon impeached Grand Secretary Mingzhu as well, again dragging in Fu.

sentences.zh: 輔入覲，亦疏訐成龍、天顏、在豐等朋比謀陷害。

translations.literal: When Fu came to audience he also memorialized accusing Chenglong, Tianyan, Zaifeng, and others of factional collusion to plot his ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu appeared at court and countered that Chenglong, Tianyan, and Zaifeng were in league to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「輔為總河，挑河築堤，漕運無誤，不可謂無功；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "As river chief, Fu has dredged rivers and built dikes; grain transport has not been disrupted—he cannot be said to have no merit;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "As river chief Fu has dredged and diked; transport has not failed—he is not without merit;

sentences.zh: 但屯田、下河二事，亦難逃罪。

translations.literal: but on the two matters of colonization and the lower river, guilt is also hard to escape.
translations.idiomatic: yet on colonization and the lower river he is hardly blameless.

sentences.zh: 近因被劾，論其過者甚多。

translations.literal: Recently, because he has been impeached, those who discuss his faults are many.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached as he is, accusers are many.

sentences.zh: 人窮則呼天，輔若不陳辨朕前，復何所控告耶？

translations.literal: When men are desperate they cry to Heaven; if Fu will not plead his case before Me, where else can he appeal?
translations.idiomatic: Desperate men cry to Heaven—if Fu will not speak before me, to whom can he appeal?

sentences.zh: 」三月，上御乾清門，召輔與成龍、琇等廷辨，輔、成龍各持所見不相下。

translations.literal: " In the third month the emperor presided at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, summoned Fu, Chenglong, Xiu, and others for court debate; Fu and Chenglong each held to his view and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor held court at the Gate of Heavenly Purity with Fu, Chenglong, and Xiu; Fu and Chenglong would not budge.

sentences.zh: 琇言輔屯田害民，輔言屬吏奉行不善致民怨，因引咎，坐罷，以王新命代，佛倫、訥、在豐、達奇納皆左遷，天顏、吉士並奪官，陳潢亦坐譴。

translations.literal: Xiu said Fu's colonization harmed the people; Fu said subordinate officials had executed orders poorly and caused popular resentment; he took blame upon himself and was dismissed; Wang Xinming replaced him; Folun, Ne, Zaifeng, and Daqina were all demoted; Tianyan and Jishi were both stripped of office; Chen Huang was also punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu charged that Fu's colonization hurt the people; Fu blamed bad execution by subordinates, accepted guilt, and was dismissed—Wang Xinming took his post; Folun, Ne, Zaifeng, and Daqina were demoted; Tianyan and Jishi were stripped; Chen Huang was punished too.

sentences.zh: 時中河工初竣，上遣學士開音布、侍衛馬武往勘，還奏中河商賈舟楫不絕。

translations.literal: At that time the Middle River works had just been completed; the emperor sent Academician Kaiyinbu and guard Ma Wu to inspect; they returned and reported merchant and trade boats unceasing on the Middle River.
translations.idiomatic: The Middle River had just been finished; Kaiyinbu and guard Ma Wu inspected it and reported merchant traffic steady on the new channel.

sentences.zh: 上諭廷臣曰：「前者於成龍奏河道為靳輔所壞，今開音布等還奏，數年未嘗衝決，漕運亦不誤。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the court: "Earlier, when Chenglong memorialized that the river channel had been ruined by Jin Fu, now that Kaiyinbu and the others have returned and reported, in several years there has not been a breach and grain transport has not been disrupted.
translations.idiomatic: He told the court: "Chenglong once said Jin Fu had ruined the channel; Kaiyinbu now reports years without a breach and transport on schedule.

sentences.zh: 若謂輔治河全無所裨，微特輔不服，即朕亦不愜。

translations.literal: If one says Fu's river work was wholly without benefit, not only will Fu be unconvinced—even I will not be satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: To say Fu's work accomplished nothing—Fu would not accept it, and neither do I.

sentences.zh: 」因遣尚書張玉書、圖納，左都御史馬齊，侍郎成其範、徐廷璽閱工，遍察輔所繕治，孰為當改，孰為不當改，詳勘具奏。

translations.literal: " He therefore sent Ministers Zhang Yushu and Tuna, Censor-in-Chief Ma Qi, and Vice Ministers Cheng Qifan and Xu Tingxi to inspect the works, thoroughly examine what Fu had repaired, determine what should be changed and what should not, survey in detail, and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Yushu, Tuna, Ma Qi, Cheng Qifan, and Xu Tingxi to review everything Fu had built and report what to keep and what to change.

sentences.zh: 玉書等還言河身漸次刷深，黃水汎溜入海，兩岸閘壩有應循舊者，有應移改者，多守輔舊規。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yushu and the others returned, they said the river channel was gradually being scoured deeper, Yellow water was spreading and flowing out to sea, and among sluices and dams on both banks some should follow the old plan and some should be moved or altered—mostly they kept to Fu's original rules.
translations.idiomatic: They returned reporting the channel deepening, Yellow water running to sea, and sluices mostly left on Fu's plan—some to be kept, a few moved.

sentences.zh: 十一月，上遣尚書蘇赫等閱通州運河，命輔偕往，請於沙河建閘蓄水，通州下流築堤束水，從之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the emperor sent Minister Su He and others to inspect the Tongzhou section of the Grand Canal and ordered Fu to accompany them; Fu requested building a sluice at Sha River to store water and dikes below Tongzhou to confine the water—the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Su He inspected the Tongzhou canal with Fu, who proposed a sluice on the Sha River to impound water and dikes below Tongzhou to confine it—approved.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，上南巡閱河，輔扈行。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year, on his southern tour to inspect the river, Fu accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year twenty-eight (1689), on a southern tour to inspect the river, Fu went with him.

sentences.zh: 閱中河，上慮逼近黃河，水漲堤潰；

translations.literal: Inspecting the Middle River, the emperor worried that it lay close to the Yellow River and that when water rose the dike might burst;
translations.idiomatic: At the Middle River the emperor feared its proximity to the Yellow—if the river rose, the dike might fail;

sentences.zh: 輔對若加築遙堤即無患。

translations.literal: Fu replied that if a distant dike were added there would be no danger.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said a distant dike would remove the risk.

sentences.zh: 還京師，諭獎輔所繕治河深堤固，命還舊秩。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he praised the depth of the river and solidity of the dikes Fu had repaired and ordered his former rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing he praised Fu's deep channel and solid dikes and restored his former rank.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，漕運總督董訥以北運河水淺，擬盡引南旺河水北流；

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Grain Transport Director Dong Ne, because the north canal's water was shallow, proposed drawing all the water of Nanwang Lake northward;
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-nine (1690), Transport Director Dong Ne, finding the north canal shallow, proposed diverting all Nanwang Lake water north;

sentences.zh: 倉場侍郎開音布复疏請濬北運河。

translations.literal: Granary Vice Minister Kaiyinbu again memorialized requesting dredging of the north canal.
translations.idiomatic: Granary Vice Minister Kaiyinbu again asked to dredge the north canal.

sentences.zh: 上諮輔，言南旺河水盡北流，南河必水淺，惟從北河兩旁下埽束水，自可濟運。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted Fu, who said that if all Nanwang water flowed north the south canal would certainly run shallow; only by laying fascines along both sides of the north canal to confine the water could transport be aided.
translations.idiomatic: Consulting Fu, he said sending all Nanwang water north would shallow the south canal; fascines along the north canal banks would suffice for transport.

sentences.zh: 上命偕開音布董理。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to direct the work together with Kaiyinbu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fu and Kaiyinbu to manage it together.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，王新命坐事罷，上曰：「朕聽政後，以三籓及河務、漕運為三大事，書宮中柱上。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, Wang Xinming was dismissed for an offense; the emperor said: "After I began to rule, I took the Three Feudatories, river affairs, and grain transport as the three great affairs and wrote them on pillars in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-one (1692), Wang Xinming was dismissed; the emperor said: "When I took power I wrote the Three Feudatories, river work, and grain transport on the palace pillars as the three great affairs.

sentences.zh: 河務不得其人，必誤漕運。

translations.literal: If river affairs do not have the right man, grain transport will certainly be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Without the right man on the river, transport will fail.

sentences.zh: 及輔未甚老而用之，亦得紓數年之慮。

translations.literal: Employ Fu while he is not yet very old and one can also ease several years of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Recall Fu while he is not too old and years of worry may ease.

sentences.zh: 」令仍為河道總督，輔以衰弱辭，命順天府丞徐廷璽為協理。

translations.literal: " He ordered Fu again made Director-General of River Works; Fu declined on grounds of weakness; Xu Tingxi, Vice Director of Shuntian Prefecture, was appointed as assistant manager.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was reappointed river chief; he pleaded infirmity; Shuntian Vice Director Xu Tingxi was named to assist.

sentences.zh: 會陝西西安、鳳翔災，上命留江北漕糧二十萬石，自黃河運蒲州。

translations.literal: When Xi'an and Fengxiang in Shaanxi suffered disaster, the emperor ordered two hundred thousand shi of Jiangbei grain transport retained and shipped from the Yellow River to Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster struck Xi'an and Fengxiang in Shaanxi; the emperor held back two hundred thousand shi of Jiangbei grain to ship up the Yellow River to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 輔疏言水道止可至孟津，親詣督運，上嘉之。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized that the water route could reach only as far as Mengjin; he would go in person to supervise transport; the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu reported the waterway reached only to Mengjin and that he would supervise transport in person; the emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 輔疏請就高家堰運料小河培堤使高廣，中河加築遙堤，並增建四閘，堵塞張莊舊運口，皆前此繕治所未竟者。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized requesting that the material-transport channel at Gaojiayan be used to raise and widen the dike, that a distant dike be added on the Middle River, that four additional sluices be built, and that the old transport mouth at Zhangzhuang be sealed—all unfinished items from earlier repairs.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to raise Gaojiayan's material channel and dikes, add a distant dike on the Middle River, build four more sluices, and close the old Zhangzhuang mouth—all work left unfinished.

sentences.zh: 別疏請復陳潢官，並起用熊一瀟、達奇納、趙吉士。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he asked that Chen Huang's office be restored and that Xiong Yixiao, Daqina, and Zhao Jishi be reemployed.
translations.idiomatic: He separately asked to restore Chen Huang and recall Xiong Yixiao, Daqina, and Zhao Jishi.

sentences.zh: 輔病劇，再疏乞解任，命內大臣明珠往視，傳諭調治。

translations.literal: Fu's illness grew severe; he memorialized again begging to be released from office; the emperor ordered Inner Minister Mingzhu to visit him and conveyed orders for him to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: Gravely ill, Fu again begged to resign; the emperor sent Mingzhu to visit and ordered him to rest and recover.

sentences.zh: 十一月，卒，賜祭葬，諡文襄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died; funeral sacrifices were granted and his posthumous title was Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month; the court granted funeral rites and the posthumous title Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，允江南士民請，建祠河干。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, granting the request of Jiangnan scholars and commoners, a shrine was built on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-five (1696), at the plea of Jiangnan gentry and people, a shrine was raised on the riverbank for him.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，追贈太子太保，予拜他喇布勒哈番世職。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted a hereditary baitalahabulehaikan rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-six (1707) he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given a hereditary baitalahabulehaikan office.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，復加工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, again promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongzheng (1727) he was again given the posthumous rank of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子治豫，襲職。

translations.literal: His son Zhi Yu inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi Yu succeeded to the hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 世宗以其侍父在官，知河務，命自副參領加工部侍郎銜，協理江南河工。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor, because he had attended his father in office and knew river affairs, ordered him to rise from Associate Brigade Commander with the concurrent rank of Vice Minister of Works and to assist in managing Jiangnan river works.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor, finding that he had served at his father's side and understood river work, ordered him promoted from Associate Brigade Commander with the concurrent title of Vice Minister of Works to help manage Jiangnan river projects.

sentences.zh: 陳潢，字天一，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Chen Huang, styled Tianyi, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huang, styled Tianyi, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 負才久不遇，過邯鄲呂祖祠，題詩壁間，語豪邁。

translations.literal: Talented but long without appointment, passing the Lü Ancestor Temple at Handan he inscribed a poem on the wall—language bold and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted yet long unemployed, he passed the Lüzu Temple at Handan and wrote a poem on its wall in a voice proud and expansive.

sentences.zh: 輔見而異焉，踪跡得之，引為幕客，甚相得。

translations.literal: Fu saw it and marveled; tracking him down he took him as a staff adviser—they were extremely compatible.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu read it and was struck; he traced Huang down, brought him onto his staff, and they suited each other exceedingly well.

sentences.zh: 凡輔所建白，多自潢發之。

translations.literal: Most of what Fu proposed originated with Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly every proposal Fu put forward had its start in Huang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年，上巡河，問輔：「孰為汝佐？

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi, the emperor toured the river and asked Fu: "Who assists you?
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year twenty-three (1684), the emperor inspected the river works and asked Fu, "Who is your right hand?

sentences.zh: 」以潢對。

translations.literal: " He answered with Huang.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu named Huang.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，輔疏言潢十年佐治勤勞，下部議，授潢僉事道銜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Fu memorialized that Huang had assisted in governance with diligence for ten years; the ministry deliberated and Huang was given the rank of Secretariat Participant.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six (1687) Fu reported Huang's ten years of tireless assistance; the ministries reviewed the case and Huang received the rank of Secretariat Participant.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，郭琇劾輔，辭連潢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Guo Xiu impeached Fu, and his accusation implicated Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-seven (1688) Guo Xiu attacked Fu, and his charges dragged in Huang as well.

sentences.zh: 輔罷，潢削職銜，逮京師，未入獄，以病卒。

translations.literal: Fu was dismissed; Huang was stripped of rank, escorted to the capital, had not yet entered prison when he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Fu fell from office; Huang lost his rank, was brought to Beijing, and died of illness before he ever saw a jail.

sentences.zh: 輔復起，疏請復潢官，部議以潢已卒，寢其奏。

translations.literal: When Fu was reappointed he memorialized to restore Huang's office; the ministry ruled that since Huang was already dead, the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu returned to power he asked that Huang's rank be restored; the ministries held that Huang was already dead and let the petition die.

sentences.zh: 潢佐治河，主順河性而利導之，有所患必推其致患之由；

translations.literal: Huang in assisting river control held that one should follow the river's nature and guide it advantageously; whenever there was trouble he traced its cause;
translations.idiomatic: In river work Huang held that one must follow the river's nature and steer it to advantage; whenever trouble arose he traced it to its source;

sentences.zh: 工主覈實，料主豫備，而估計不當過省，省則速敗，所費較所省尤大；

translations.literal: works demanded verification on the ground, materials foresight in stockpiling, and estimates must not be overly stingy—for stinginess brings swift failure and the cost exceeds what was saved;
translations.idiomatic: projects required on-site verification, supplies advance provisioning, and budgets must not be pared too thin—parsimony fails fast, and the repair costs more than the savings;

sentences.zh: 慎固堤防，主潘季馴束水刷沙之說，尤以減水壩為要務；

translations.literal: dike defense must be careful and solid; he upheld Pan Jixun's doctrine of binding water to scour silt, especially stressing spillway dams as essential;
translations.idiomatic: dikes had to be strengthened with care; he followed Pan Jixun's teaching that confined water scours silt, and above all treated flood-relief dams as vital;

sentences.zh: 有潰決，先固兩旁，不使日擴，乃修復故道，而疏引河以注之；

translations.literal: when breaches occurred, first secure both flanks so they would not widen day by day, then restore the old channel and cut branch streams to feed it;
translations.idiomatic: when a breach opened, he first shored both sides so it would not widen day by day, then reopened the old course and cut feeder channels to draw water in;

sentences.zh: 河流今昔形勢不同，無一勞永逸之策，在時時謹小慎微，而尤重在河員之久任。

translations.literal: river courses differ past and present—there is no once-for-all policy; what matters is constant minute care, and above all long tenure for river officials.
translations.idiomatic: rivers change shape from age to age—no policy lasts forever; success lay in unceasing small vigilance, and most of all in keeping river officers long in post.

sentences.zh: 張靄生採潢所論，次為治河述言十二篇。

translations.literal: Zhang Aisheng collected Huang's discussions and arranged them into twelve chapters of Discourses on River Control.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Aisheng gathered Huang's views and arranged them into twelve chapters entitled Discourses on River Control.

sentences.zh: 高宗以靄生河圖能得真源，命採其書入四庫，與輔治河奏績並列。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor, because Aisheng's river maps grasped true sources, ordered the book taken into the Siku Quanshu, listed alongside Fu's achievements in river control.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor, judging Aisheng's river maps true to their sources, ordered the work into the Siku Quanshu, ranking it with Fu's record of river victories.

sentences.zh: 宋文運，字開之，直隸南宮人。

translations.literal: Song Wenyun, styled Kaizhi, was a native of Nangong in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wenyun, styled Kaizhi, was from Nangong in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，授山東滋陽知縣，行取刑部主事。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, appointed magistrate of Ziyang in Shandong, selected as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi year six (1649), he became magistrate of Ziyang in Shandong and was then tapped as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部郎中，掌選政，清直守正。

translations.literal: Promoted twice to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, in charge of appointments—upright and scrupulous.
translations.idiomatic: Twice promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, he held the power of appointments with clean, upright integrity.

sentences.zh: 以魏象樞薦，擢鴻臚寺少卿，累擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: On Wei Xiangshu's recommendation he was raised to Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and eventually Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiangshu recommended him; he rose to Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and eventually to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 命佐伊桑阿行河，上特諭之曰：「爾有所見，當堅持詳議，毋以伊桑阿為尚書而阿其意也。

translations.literal: Ordered to assist Yisang'a on river inspection, the emperor specially instructed him: "What you see, hold firmly to and debate in detail; do not defer to Yisang'a because he is a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to assist Yisang'a on river inspection, he received a special order: "Hold to your own views and argue them through; do not yield to Yisang'a simply because he is a minister.

sentences.zh: 」以病乞休，加太子少保，致仕。

translations.literal: " He begged leave on grounds of illness; made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: " He retired on grounds of illness, was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and left office.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡端愨。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Duanque.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Duanque.

sentences.zh: 久之，上猶謂文選司事要，文運操守聲名，無能及之者。

translations.literal: Long afterward the emperor still said that affairs of the Personnel Selection Bureau were critical, and that in integrity and reputation none could equal Wenyun.
translations.idiomatic: Long after his death the emperor still said the Selection Bureau's business was vital, and that in integrity and fame no one matched Wenyun.

sentences.zh: 董訥，字茲重，山東平原人。

translations.literal: Dong Ne, styled Zizhong, was a native of Pingyuan in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ne, styled Zizhong, came from Pingyuan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he placed third among the first-rank jinshi and was made a compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year six (1667) he took third place among the top jinshi and entered the Hanlin as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 累擢至江南總督。

translations.literal: He rose to Governor-General of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Governor-General of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 為政持大體，有惠於民。

translations.literal: In government he grasped the large design and brought benefit to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He governed for the broad design and did real good for the people.

sentences.zh: 左遷去，江南民為立生祠。

translations.literal: After demotion and departure, Jiangnan people built him a living shrine.
translations.idiomatic: After his demotion and departure, the people of Jiangnan built him a living shrine.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上南巡，民執香跪訥生祠前，求復官訥江南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor toured south; the people held incense and knelt before Ne's shrine, begging that Ne be restored to office in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight (1689), during the southern tour, people knelt with incense before Ne's shrine and begged that he be sent back to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 上還蹕，笑謂訥曰：「汝官江南惠及民，民為汝建小廟。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he laughed and said to Ne: "Your service in Jiangnan benefited the people—the people built you a small temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey the emperor laughed and told Ne, "Your tenure in Jiangnan helped the people—they have built you a little temple.

sentences.zh: 」旋以侍讀學士復出為漕運總督。

translations.literal: " Soon he was sent out again as Governor of Grain Transport with the rank of Reader of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was sent out again as Grain Transport Governor with the rank of Hanlin Reader.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 熊一瀟，字蔚懷，江西南昌人。

translations.literal: Xiong Yixiao, styled Weihuai, was a native of Nanchang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yixiao, styled Weihuai, was a native of Nanchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年進士，改庶吉士，授浙江道監察御史。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the third year of Kangxi, transferred to Hanlin bachelor, appointed Censor of the Zhejiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Kangxi year three (1664), he became a Hanlin bachelor and then Censor of the Zhejiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 請罷投誠武官改授文官例，並議裁併各關，皆下部議行。

translations.literal: He petitioned to abolish the rule transferring surrendered military officers to civil posts, and also proposed merging customs stations—both referred to the ministries and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to end the practice of turning surrendered military officers into civil officials and proposed merging customs posts; both went to the ministries and were carried out.

sentences.zh: 累官工部尚書，坐奪官。

translations.literal: He eventually reached Minister of Works, then was dismissed and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Works, then was dismissed and stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 以輔遺疏薦，起太常寺卿，復至工部尚書。

translations.literal: On Fu's posthumous memorial recommending him, he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and again reached Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On Fu's deathbed recommendation he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and again rose to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died.

sentences.zh: 孫學鵬，進士，官廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: His grandson Sun Xuepeng, a jinshi, served as Governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Sun Xuepeng, a jinshi, became Governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 於成龍，字振甲，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong, styled Zhenjia, belonged to the Han Military Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong, styled Zhenjia, belonged to the Han Military Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，自廕生授直隸樂亭知縣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi, from yinsheng he was appointed magistrate of Leting in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year seven (1668), through hereditary privilege he was made magistrate of Leting in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 八年，署灤州知州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he acted as prefect of Luanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight (1669) he served as acting prefect of Luanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以逸囚當降調，樂亭民列善政，兩叩閽籥留，下巡撫金世德勘實，得復任。

translations.literal: For letting prisoners escape he should have been demoted; Leting people listed his good policies and twice knocked on the palace gate to keep him; the Zhili governor Jin Shide investigated and confirmed, and he was reinstated.
translations.idiomatic: When escaped prisoners cost him a demotion, the people of Leting catalogued his good rule and twice battered the palace gates to keep him; Governor Jin Shide verified the facts and he kept his post.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以緝盜逾限未獲，又當降調，世德疏請留，上特許之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, for failing to capture bandits within the time limit he should again have been demoted; Jin Shide memorialized to retain him, and the emperor specially permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen (1674), failure to catch bandits within the deadline again called for demotion; Jin Shide memorialized to keep him, and the emperor granted an exception.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷通州知州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen (1679) he was moved to prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年，直隸巡撫於成龍遷兩江總督，疏薦可大用；

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Yu Chenglong, Governor of Zhili, moved to Governor-General of Liangjiang and memorialized recommending great appointment;
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty (1681), Yu Chenglong, now Governor of Zhili, was shifted to Governor-General of Liangjiang and memorialized that he was fit for greater trust;

sentences.zh: 會江寧府缺員，疏請敕廷臣推清操久著與相類者，上即以命成龍。

translations.literal: when Jiangning prefecture fell vacant he memorialized asking the throne to have ministers recommend officials of longstanding pure conduct like himself, and the emperor directly appointed Yu Chenglong.
translations.idiomatic: when Jiangning prefect fell vacant he asked the throne to name an official of long-proven integrity like himself—and the emperor appointed Yu Chenglong.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，上南巡至江寧，嘉成龍廉潔，親書手捲賜之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the emperor's southern tour reached Jiangning; he praised Yu Chenglong's integrity and personally wrote a handscroll to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three (1684), on the southern tour at Jiangning, the emperor praised Chenglong's integrity and wrote a handscroll with his own brush as a gift.

sentences.zh: 超擢安徽按察使。

translations.literal: He was abruptly promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was abruptly promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 上還京師，賜其父參領得水貂裘，並諭八旗諸大臣有子弟為外吏者，各貽書訓勉，視得水之教成龍。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital he gave Chenglong's father, Colonel Deshui, a water-marten robe, and told all Eight Banner ministers whose sons were outer officials to send letters of instruction, taking Deshui's teaching of Chenglong as the model.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing the emperor gave Chenglong's father, Colonel Yu Deshui, a robe of water marten, and told every Eight Banner minister with a son in provincial service to write home in admonition, holding up Deshui's rearing of Chenglong as the standard.

sentences.zh: 上以江南下河諸州縣久被水，敕議疏濬，命成龍分理，仍聽河道總督靳輔節制。

translations.literal: Because the lower-river districts of Jiangnan had long suffered flood, the emperor ordered plans for dredging and put Chenglong in charge, still under Director-General Jin Fu's command.
translations.idiomatic: With the lower-river counties of Jiangnan long drowned, the emperor ordered dredging discussed and set Chenglong to it, still under Director-General Jin Fu.

sentences.zh: 輔請於上流築堤束水；

translations.literal: Fu requested building dikes upstream to bind the water;
translations.idiomatic: Fu proposed upstream dikes to confine the current;

sentences.zh: 成龍擬疏海口，濬下河水道，持異議。

translations.literal: Chenglong proposed dredging the sea mouth and the lower-river channels, and held a dissenting view.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong favored dredging the sea mouth and the lower-river channels, and the two men split.

sentences.zh: 上遣尚書薩穆哈、學士穆稱額往諮於民，薩穆哈等還奏，言眾謂濬海無益，乃命緩興工。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister Samuha and Academician Much'a'e to consult the people; when Samuha and the others returned they reported that the masses said dredging the sea was useless, and work was ordered suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister Samuha and Academician Much'a'e to ask the people; they came back saying folk believed dredging the sea would not help, and construction was postponed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年二月，授成龍直隸巡撫。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fifth year Chenglong was appointed Governor of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year twenty-five (1686) Chenglong was made Governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 入對，上問：「治畿輔利弊應興革者宜何先？

translations.literal: On entering audience the emperor asked: "In governing the capital region, what benefits and harms should be promoted or reformed first?
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor asked, "Governing the capital province—what should be reformed or advanced first?

sentences.zh: 」成龍對：「弭盜為先。

translations.literal: " Chenglong answered: "Suppressing bandits comes first.
translations.idiomatic: " Chenglong replied, "Put down banditry first.

sentences.zh: 姦宄倚旗下為淵藪，有司莫敢誰何，臣當執法治之。

translations.literal: Evildoers rely on the Banners as lairs; local officials dare not challenge them—I shall enforce the law upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals hide behind Banner privilege; magistrates dare not touch them—I mean to apply the law.

sentences.zh: 」瀕行，賜白金千、表里二十端。

translations.literal: " On the verge of departure he was granted a thousand taels of silver and twenty rolls of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " As he left he received a thousand taels of silver and twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 上官，疏言：「弭盜當力行保甲，旗下莊屯不屬於州縣，本旗統領遠在京師，僅有撥什庫在屯，未能約束。

translations.literal: On taking office he memorialized: "To suppress bandits the baojia system must be vigorously enforced; Banner estate colonies do not fall under prefectures and counties, their banner commanders are far off in the capital, and only dispatched clerks remain in the colonies—they cannot restrain anyone.
translations.idiomatic: In his first memorial he wrote: "Banditry yields only to strict baojia; Banner estates lie outside county jurisdiction, their commanders sit in Beijing, and a few dispatched clerks in the fields cannot keep order.

sentences.zh: 應令旗人與民戶同編保甲，撥什庫、鄉長互相稽察，盜發，無問所劫為旗為民，協力救護。

translations.literal: Banner people and civilian households should be enrolled in the same baojia; dispatched clerks and village heads should check one another; when robbery occurs, regardless whether the victim is Banner or civilian, all should aid in rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Register Banner families and commoners in the same baojia; let dispatched clerks and village heads watch each other; when robbery strikes, whether the victim wears the banner or not, neighbors must rally to help.

sentences.zh: 得盜，賞；

translations.literal: Capture a bandit, reward;
translations.idiomatic: Catch a thief—reward;

sentences.zh: 藏盜、縱盜，罰。

translations.literal: harbor or abet a bandit, punish.
translations.idiomatic: hide or shelter one—punish.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「燕山六衛，所轄遼闊，與州縣不相統屬，盜發止責汛弁捕治，而衛官置不問。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "The six guards of Yanshan govern vast territory without belonging to prefectures and counties; when bandits appear only the river-defense deputies are charged with capture, while the guard officers pay no heed.
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "The six Yanshan guards span country that answers to no county; when thieves rise only river-defense deputies are told to hunt them, while guard officers look away.

sentences.zh: 請以衛地屬所近州縣同編保甲，並於通州、盧溝橋、黃村、沙河各設捕盜同知，守備以下分汛、墩、台及旗下莊屯，悉歸稽察。

translations.literal: Ask that guard lands be attached to the nearest prefectures and counties for joint baojia enrollment, and that bandit-catching sub-prefects be set up at Tongzhou, Lugou Bridge, Huangcun, and Shahe; all river-defense posts, beacon towers, and Banner estates should fall under their oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Attach guard lands to neighboring counties for shared baojia; station bandit-catching sub-prefects at Tongzhou, Lugou Bridge, Huangcun, and Shahe; and bring every post, beacon, and Banner estate under their watch.

sentences.zh: 」並下部議行。

translations.literal: " Both were referred to the ministries and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: " Both proposals went to the ministries and were adopted.

sentences.zh: 先後捕治旗丁沈顛、太監張進升及大盜司九、張破樓子等，置於法。

translations.literal: In succession he captured and punished the Banner soldier Shen Dian, the eunuch Zhang Jinsheng, and the great bandits Si Jiu, Zhang Polouzi, and others, and dealt with them by law.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to seize the Bannerman Shen Dian, the eunuch Zhang Jinsheng, and master thieves such as Si Jiu and Zhang Polouzi, and punished them to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，上獎成龍廉能，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor praised Chenglong's integrity and ability and made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six (1687) the emperor commended Chenglong's honesty and competence and made him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 幸霸州，成龍朝行在，賜白金千、馬俱黃鞍轡。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Bazhou, Chenglong attended at the traveling palace and was granted a thousand taels of silver and horses with yellow saddles and bridles.
translations.idiomatic: During a visit to Bazhou, Chenglong attended at the traveling palace and received a thousand taels of silver and horses caparisoned in yellow.

sentences.zh: 湖廣巡撫張汧以貪被劾，命與副都御史開音布、山西​​巡撫馬齊往按，得實，論如律。

translations.literal: Huguang Governor Zhang Qian was impeached for greed; Chenglong was ordered to join Vice Censor-in-Chief Kaiyinbu and Shanxi Governor Ma Qi to investigate; the charges proved true and he was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When Huguang Governor Zhang Qian was impeached for corruption, Chenglong joined Vice Censor-in-Chief Kaiyinbu and Shanxi Governor Ma Qi on the investigation; guilt was established and Zhang was sentenced as the law required.

sentences.zh: 初，成龍分理下河，未興工而罷。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chenglong had managed the lower river, work had not begun before it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Chenglong had been put over the lower river, dredging never started before the project was shelved.

sentences.zh: 上又以湯斌言，復命濬治，以侍郎孫在豐董其役。

translations.literal: The emperor again, on Tang Bin's word, ordered dredging resumed and appointed Vice Minister Sun Zaifeng to direct the labor.
translations.idiomatic: On Tang Bin's advice the emperor ordered dredging resumed and put Vice Minister Sun Zaifeng in charge of the works.

sentences.zh: 輔仍主重堤束水，並議開中河，疏攔馬河減水壩所洩水。

translations.literal: Fu still advocated a heavy dike to bind the water, and also proposed opening the Middle River and dredging the water spilled from the Lanma River spillway dam.
translations.idiomatic: Fu still pressed for a heavy dike to confine the current, proposed opening the Middle River, and wanted to channel water from the Lanma River spillway dam.

sentences.zh: 上命學士禪布以疏示成龍，成龍力主濬下河，罷築重堤，並謂中河雖開無益。

translations.literal: The emperor had Academician Tanbu show the memorial to Chenglong; Chenglong strongly upheld dredging the lower river, opposed building the heavy dike, and said that even if the Middle River were opened it would do no good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Academician Tanbu show the plan to Chenglong; Chenglong still insisted on opening the lower river, opposed the heavy dike, and argued the Middle River would help nothing.

sentences.zh: 輔詣京師，疏言在豐及總漕慕天顏附和成龍，朋謀陷害。

translations.literal: Fu came to the capital and memorialized that Zaifeng and Grain Transport Director Mu Tianyan were echoing Chenglong in a factional plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu came to Beijing and charged that Zaifeng and Grain Transport Director Mu Tianyan were echoing Chenglong in a clique meant to ruin him.

sentences.zh: 成龍自湖廣還，上命諸臣廷辨之。

translations.literal: When Chenglong returned from Huguang the emperor ordered the ministers to debate the matter at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenglong returned from Huguang the emperor ordered a full court debate.

sentences.zh: 輔言濬海口慮倒灌，成龍言高家堰築堤，縱上流水不來，而秋雨時至，天長、六合諸水洩歸何處，故海口仍當濬。

translations.literal: Fu said dredging the sea mouth feared backflow; Chenglong said that if a heavy dike were built at Gaojiayan and the upstream current kept out, autumn rains would still come—where would the waters of Tianchang, Luhe, and the rest drain? Therefore the sea mouth must still be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: Fu warned that dredging the sea mouth risked tidal backflow; Chenglong answered that a heavy dike at Gaojiayan might block the main current, but autumn rains would still send the Tianchang, Luhe, and other streams pouring down—where would that water go? The sea mouth had to be opened.

sentences.zh: 上罷輔，代以王新命。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Fu and replaced him with Wang Xinming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Fu and replaced him with Wang Xinming.

sentences.zh: 及中河工竟，遣學士開音布、侍衛馬武閱視，還奏天顏令漕船退出中河。

translations.literal: When the Middle River works were finished, Academician Kaiyinbu and Guard Ma Wu were sent to inspect; they reported that Tianyan had grain boats leave the Middle River.
translations.idiomatic: After the Middle River was finished, Academician Kaiyinbu and Guard Ma Wu inspected the works and reported that Tianyan had ordered grain boats out of the new channel.

sentences.zh: 上逮問天顏，天顏發成龍私書，囑毋附輔。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Tianyan; Tianyan produced a private letter from Chenglong telling him not to side with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Tianyan, who produced a private letter from Chenglong telling him not to back Fu.

sentences.zh: 下廷臣議，削太子少保，降調，命留任。

translations.literal: The matter went to the ministers for deliberation; Chenglong was stripped of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and demoted, but ordered to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated; Chenglong lost his Junior Guardian rank and took a demotion, but was told to stay at his post.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷左都御史，兼鑲黃旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Left and concurrently Commandant of the Han Military Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-nine (1690) he became Left Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Commandant of the Han Military Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，新命罷，輔復為河督，旋卒，上以命成龍。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Xinming was dismissed; Fu was again made river director and soon died; the emperor gave the post to Chenglong.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-one (1692) Xinming fell; Fu returned as river chief, died soon after, and the emperor gave the post to Chenglong.

sentences.zh: 輔領帑購柳束，工部駁減，成龍覈無虛冒。

translations.literal: Fu had drawn treasury funds to buy willow fascines; the Ministry of Works cut the estimate; Chenglong audited and found no false claims.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had used treasury silver to buy willow bundles; the Ministry of Works slashed the figures; Chenglong audited the accounts and found no padding.

sentences.zh: 輔築高家堰重堤，募夫遠方，預給銀安家，工中止，未扣抵。

translations.literal: Fu had built the heavy dike at Gaojiayan, hiring laborers from afar and paying them silver in advance to settle their families; when the work stopped the advances were never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's heavy dike at Gaojiayan had hired distant laborers and paid them settling-in silver in advance; when the project halted those advances were never clawed back.

sentences.zh: 新命題銷，格部議，成龍復以請，上並與豁免。

translations.literal: Xinming had proposed writing them off; the ministry blocked it; Chenglong memorialized again, and the emperor granted exemption for all.
translations.idiomatic: Xinming had asked to write the debt off; the ministry refused; Chenglong pleaded again, and the emperor remitted the whole sum.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，召詣京師，疏言運河自通州至嶧縣，黃河自滎澤至碭山，堤卑薄者皆宜加築高厚，並高家堰諸處改石工，毛城鋪諸處疏引河，及清江浦迤下並江都、高郵諸堤工，策大舉修治。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was summoned to the capital and memorialized that from Tongzhou on the Grand Canal to Yixian, and from Xingze to Dangshan on the Yellow River, wherever dikes were low and thin they should be raised and thickened; that stone work should replace earth at Gaojiayan and elsewhere; that diversion channels should be cut at Maochengpu and elsewhere; and that works from Qingjiangpu downstream and the dikes of Jiangdu and Gaoyou called for a great campaign of repair.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-three (1694) he was called to Beijing and urged that canal dikes from Tongzhou to Yixian and Yellow River dikes from Xingze to Dangshan be raised wherever thin, that Gaojiayan and other points be faced in stone, that diversion channels be opened at Maochengpu and the like, and that everything from Qingjiangpu down through Jiangdu and Gaoyou demanded a major repair.

sentences.zh: 別疏請設道員以下各官，又計工費，請開捐例，減成核收；

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he asked to establish officials below the intendant rank, also calculated the cost of works, and asked to open a sale-of-office quota with reduced rates for verification and collection;
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he proposed new posts below the intendant level, tallied project costs, and asked to open a sale-of-rank quota with discounted verification and collection;

sentences.zh: 並推廣休革各員，上至布政使，皆得捐复。

translations.literal: and extended restoration by purchase to all dismissed officials up to provincial administration commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: and would let dismissed officials all the way up to provincial administration commissioner buy their way back into service.

sentences.zh: 上召成龍入，問：「開捐例得無累民？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Chenglong in and asked: "Opening a sale-of-office quota—will it not burden the people?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Chenglong in and asked, "Will opening sale-of-rank offices not crush the common people?

sentences.zh: 」成龍言：「無累。

translations.literal: " Chenglong said: "It will not burden them.
translations.idiomatic: " Chenglong said, "It will not.

sentences.zh: 」請益力，上廷折之，成龍乃請罪。

translations.literal: " He pressed harder; the emperor rebuked him at court, and Chenglong then begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed his case; the emperor cut him down in open court, and Chenglong begged pardon.

sentences.zh: 上因問：「爾嘗短靳輔，謂減水壩不宜開，今果何如？

translations.literal: The emperor then asked: "You once faulted Jin Fu, saying spillway dams should not be opened—how does that stand now?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked, "You once attacked Jin Fu for opening spillway dams—what do you say now?

sentences.zh: 」成龍曰：「臣彼時妄言，今亦視輔而行。

translations.literal: " Chenglong said: "Your servant spoke rashly then; now I too act according to Fu's course."
translations.idiomatic: " Chenglong said, "I spoke rashly then; now I follow Fu's lead as well."

sentences.zh: 」廷臣議成龍懷私妄奏，當奪官，上命留任。

translations.literal: " The court ministers held that Chenglong had memorialized out of private motive and rashly, and that his office should be stripped; the emperor ordered him kept in post.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers ruled that Chenglong had acted from private interest in a reckless memorial and should lose his rank; the emperor let him remain.

sentences.zh: 仍興舉簡要各工，乃請先將高家堰土堤改築石工。

translations.literal: He still urged the essential works in summary, and then asked first to rebuild the earthen dike at Gaojiayan as stone work.
translations.idiomatic: He still pressed the essential projects in brief, and asked that Gaojiayan's earthen dike be faced in stone first.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，命复官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was ordered restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-four (1695) the emperor ordered his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 旋丁父憂，還京師，以董安國代。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his father, returned to the capital, and Dong Anguo replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his father died; he returned to Beijing, and Dong Anguo took his place.

sentences.zh: 上親征噶爾丹，再出塞，命成龍以左都御史銜督餉，噶爾丹竄死，予拜他喇布勒哈番世職。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned in person against Galdan and again went beyond the pass; Chenglong was ordered to supervise provisions with the rank of Censor-in-Chief of the Left; Galdan fled and died; he was granted a hereditary tatara-bule-haifen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched in person against Galdan and again crossed the frontier; Chenglong was sent to supervise supplies as Left Censor-in-Chief; when Galdan died in flight, Chenglong was granted a hereditary tatara-bule-haifen.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，命以總督銜管直隸巡撫，請修永清、固安渾河堤，並加以濬治，上為改河名曰永定。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was ordered to oversee the Zhili governor with a governor-general's rank; he asked to repair the Hun River dikes at Yongqing and Gu'an and also dredge them; the emperor renamed the river Yongding.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-seven (1698) he was given a governor-general's rank to oversee Zhili, asked to repair and dredge the Hun River dikes at Yongqing and Gu'an, and the emperor renamed the river Yongding—"Ever Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 旋疏請設南北岸分司。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized asking to establish separate offices for the north and south banks.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized to set up separate north- and south-bank sub-offices.

sentences.zh: 董安國罷，复授河道總督。

translations.literal: Dong Anguo was dismissed; Chenglong was again appointed Director-General of Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Anguo fell, Chenglong was again made river director.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上南巡，臨閱高家堰、歸仁堤諸處，諭以增築疏濬諸事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the emperor made a southern tour, personally inspected Gaojiayan, the Guiren dike, and other places, and instructed on raising dikes, dredging, and other matters.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-eight (1699) the emperor toured the south, inspected Gaojiayan and the Guiren dike in person, and ordered work to raise and dredge the works there.

sentences.zh: 尋以病乞假，命在任調治，遣醫往視。

translations.literal: Soon, ill, he asked for leave; he was ordered to convalesce in office, and a physician was sent to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon illness drove him to ask leave; the emperor told him to recover in post and sent a physician.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，卒，賜祭葬，諡襄勤。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he died; funeral rites were granted, and his posthumous title was Xiangqin.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-nine (1700) he died; the court granted funeral honors and gave him the posthumous name Xiangqin.

sentences.zh: 孫在豐，字屺瞻，浙江德清人。

translations.literal: Sun Zaifeng, courtesy name Qizhan, was a man of Deqing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zaifeng, styled Qizhan, came from Deqing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年一甲二名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi he placed second among the first-rank jinshi and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1670 he took second place among the top jinshi and entered the Hanlin as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 直起居注，充日講官，進講屢稱旨。

translations.literal: He served at the Office of Imperial Diaries, acted as day lecturer, and his lectures often pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Diary Office, lectured before the throne, and his explanations often won the emperor's praise.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部侍郎，仍兼翰林院學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Vice Minister of Works while still holding the Hanlin academician's title.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Works while retaining his Hanlin academician rank.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，命率郎中鄂素等赴淮、揚濬海口，鑄監修下河工部印授之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was ordered to lead Director Esu and others to the Huai and Yang regions to dredge the estuary; a Ministry of Works seal for supervising lower-river repairs was cast and given him.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six (1687) he was sent with Director Esu and others to dredge the Huai-Yang estuary; the court cast a Ministry of Works seal for lower-river supervision and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 在豐疏言開新不如循舊，築高不如就低，迤遠不如取近。

translations.literal: Zaifeng memorialized that opening new channels was not as good as following the old course, building high was not as good as staying low, and going far was not as good as taking what was near.
translations.idiomatic: Zaifeng argued that new cuts were worse than the old channel, high dikes worse than low ground, and distant works worse than nearby ones.

sentences.zh: 施工以岡門鎮為最先，次白駒場，次丁溪場，次草堰。

translations.literal: Construction was to begin first at Gangmen Town, next at Baiju, then Dingxi, then Caoyan.
translations.idiomatic: Work was to start at Gangmen Town, then Baiju, Dingxi, and Caoyan in that order.

sentences.zh: 上悉從之，並以在豐請，令輔閉高家堰及高郵諸減水壩。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed to all of it, and on Zaifeng's request ordered Fu to close the spillway dams at Gaojiayan and Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the whole plan, and at Zaifeng's request ordered Fu to shut the spillway dams at Gaojiayan and Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 輔仍主築堤束水。

translations.literal: Fu still advocated building dikes to bind the water.
translations.idiomatic: Fu still pressed for dikes to confine the current.

sentences.zh: 上令輔會總督董訥、總漕慕天顏及在豐集議，遂會疏用輔議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Fu to meet with Governor-General Dong Ne, Grain Transport Director Mu Tianyan, and Zaifeng for joint deliberation; they then submitted a joint memorial adopting Fu's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Fu confer with Governor Dong Ne, Grain Transport Director Mu Tianyan, and Zaifeng; their joint memorial adopted Fu's plan.

sentences.zh: 在豐監修海口岡門鎮、白駒工已畢，丁溪、草堰工俱停。

translations.literal: Under Zaifeng's supervision the estuary works at Gangmen Town and Baiju were finished; work at Dingxi and Caoyan was all halted.
translations.idiomatic: Zaifeng finished the estuary works at Gangmen Town and Baiju; the Dingxi and Caoyan projects were stopped.

sentences.zh: 上以諮成龍，成龍言：「上遣在豐監修下河，萬民歡頌。

translations.literal: The emperor consulted Chenglong; Chenglong said: "Your Majesty sent Zaifeng to supervise repairs on the lower river, and the myriad people rejoiced and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Chenglong, who said, "Your Majesty sent Zaifeng to supervise the lower river, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 今岡門、白駒諸工將竣，而輔又以為無益，欲於高家堰等處築堤。

translations.literal: Now the works at Gangmen, Baiju, and elsewhere are nearly finished, yet Fu again thinks them useless and wants to build dikes at Gaojiayan and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Gangmen and Baiju are nearly done, yet Fu again calls the dredging useless and wants dikes at Gaojiayan instead.

sentences.zh: 在豐先經履勘，始行興工；

translations.literal: Zaifeng had first gone in person to survey on the ground before work was begun;
translations.idiomatic: Zaifeng had surveyed the ground himself before a single spade was turned;

sentences.zh: 若果無益，何待開濬年餘又會議請停？

translations.literal: if it were truly useless, why wait more than a year of dredging and then meet in council to ask that it stop?
translations.idiomatic: if the work were truly useless, why dredge for more than a year and only then meet to ask that it stop?

sentences.zh: 此實臣所不能解也。

translations.literal: This your servant truly cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: That is what I cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 」二十七年，在豐疏劾輔阻撓下河，輔亦劾在豐與天顏結姻，附和成龍。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-seventh year Zaifeng memorialized to impeach Fu for obstructing the lower river; Fu also impeached Zaifeng for marrying into Tianyan's family and echoing Chenglong.
translations.idiomatic: " In year twenty-seven (1688) Zaifeng impeached Fu for blocking the lower river; Fu impeached Zaifeng for marrying into Tianyan's family and siding with Chenglong.

sentences.zh: 下廷臣議，輔罷，成龍坐鐫秩，責在豐前後言不仇，降調。

translations.literal: The matter went to the ministers for deliberation: Fu was dismissed; Chenglong was demoted one rank; Zaifeng was faulted because his earlier and later statements did not agree, and was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated: Fu fell; Chenglong lost one rank; Zaifeng was faulted for contradicting himself and demoted.

sentences.zh: 上命仍以翰林官用，俄授侍讀學士。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that he still be used as a Hanlin official; soon he was made Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept him in Hanlin service and soon made him Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight (1689) he became a Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 開音布，西林覺羅氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Kaiyinbu, of the Xilin Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyinbu, of the Xilin Gioro clan, belonged to the Manchu Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式授內閣中書，累遷至左副都御史。

translations.literal: From clerk of the fourth rank he was appointed Grand Secretariat secretary and rose step by step to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from clerk to Grand Secretariat secretary and eventually to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十六年，偕成龍按湖廣巡撫張汧，論罪如律。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Kangxi, together with Chenglong he investigated Huguang Governor Zhang Qian; guilt was determined according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1687 he and Chenglong investigated Huguang Governor Zhang Qian and punished him according to law.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，擢戶部侍郎，命監理高郵、寶應下河工程。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and ordered to supervise the lower-river works at Gaoyou and Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-seven (1688) he became Vice Minister of Revenue and was put in charge of the lower-river works at Gaoyou and Baoying.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上南巡，成龍扈行，命與侍郎徐廷璽閱視下河，還奏丁溪至白駒，水三道入海，上流馮家壩引河當仍開濬，餘工悉可停。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, on the emperor's southern tour, Chenglong attended him; Kaiyinbu was ordered with Vice Minister Xu Tingxi to inspect the lower river and reported that from Dingxi to Baiju water ran in three channels to the sea, that the diversion channel at Fengjiaba upstream should still be dredged, and that the remaining works could all be halted.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight (1689), on the southern tour, Chenglong attended the emperor; Kaiyinbu and Vice Minister Xu Tingxi inspected the lower river and reported that from Dingxi to Baiju three channels reached the sea, that Fengjiaba's diversion upstream still needed dredging, and that the rest of the work could stop.

sentences.zh: 乃召開音布還，授正白旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: Kaiyinbu was then recalled and appointed Manchu vice commandant of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyinbu was recalled and made Manchu vice commandant of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 尋擢步軍統領，遷兵部尚書，授鑲白旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Metropolitan Brigade commander, transferred to Minister of War, and appointed commandant of the Manchu Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Metropolitan Brigade commander, then Minister of War, and commandant of the Manchu Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，命專管步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was ordered to manage the Metropolitan Brigade exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-eight (1699) he was ordered to manage the Metropolitan Brigade alone.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，卒，諡肅敏。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he died; his posthumous title was Sumin.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-one (1702) he died, with the posthumous name Sumin.

sentences.zh: 張鵬翮，字運青，四川遂寧人。

translations.literal: Zhang Penghe, courtesy name Yunqing, was a man of Suining in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Penghe, styled Yunqing, came from Suining in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination and was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1670 and entered the Hanlin as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 改刑部主事，累遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and rose step by step to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of Punishments and rose to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授江南蘇州知府，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed prefect of Suzhou in Jiangnan and entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen (1680) he became prefect of Suzhou in Jiangnan, then mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 除山東兗州知府，舉卓異，擢河東鹽運使，內遷通政司參議，轉兵部督捕副理事官。

translations.literal: On leaving mourning he became prefect of Yanzhou in Shandong, was cited for outstanding merit, was promoted salt transport commissioner of Hedong, was transferred within the capital to vice commissioner of the Court of Transmission, and then became vice director of military pursuit in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as prefect of Yanzhou in Shandong, won an outstanding-merit citation, became Hedong salt commissioner, then moved to the Court of Transmission and the Ministry of War's pursuit office.

sentences.zh: 從內大臣索額圖等勘定俄羅斯界，還擢大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Ministers such as Songgotu to survey and fix the Russian border; on return he was promoted to vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
