translations.idiomatic: He joined Grand Minister Songgotu and others in fixing the Russian border, then became vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight (1689) he became governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 疏言紳民原畝捐穀四合，力不能者聽。

translations.literal: He memorialized that gentry and commoners should donate four he of grain per original mu, and that those unable were to be excused.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that gentry and commoners donate four he of grain per registered mu, with exemption for those who could not pay.

sentences.zh: 旋以杭州、嘉興等府秋收歉薄，請暫免輸穀。

translations.literal: Soon, because the autumn harvest was thin in Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and other prefectures, he asked that grain payments be temporarily waived.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and other prefectures reported a poor autumn harvest, he asked to suspend the grain levy.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「昨歲浙江被災，循例蠲賦，並豁免錢糧，豈可強令捐輸？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Last year Zhejiang suffered disaster; land tax was remitted by precedent, and money and grain dues were also exempted—how can they be forced to donate?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhejiang was stricken last year; land tax was remitted by precedent and money and grain dues waived—how can you force donations?

sentences.zh: 鵬翮原題力不能者聽，自相矛盾。

translations.literal: Penghe's original memorial said those unable were to be excused; this contradicts itself.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe's own memorial said the unable were excused—this contradicts itself.

sentences.zh: 」下部議，奪官，上寬之。

translations.literal: " The matter went to the ministries for deliberation; his office was to be stripped, but the emperor showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministries ruled he should lose his post; the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部侍郎，督江南學政。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of War and superintendent of education in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Vice Minister of War and Jiangnan education superintendent.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-six (1697) he became Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，遷刑部尚書，授江南江西總督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to Minister of Punishments and appointed governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-seven (1698) he became Minister of Punishments and governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上南巡，命鵬翮扈從入京，賜朝服、鞍馬、弓矢。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, on the emperor's southern tour, Penghe was ordered to attend him into the capital and was granted court dress, saddle horse, bow, and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-eight (1699), on the southern tour, Penghe was brought to Beijing in the imperial retinue and given court dress, a horse, bow, and arrows.

sentences.zh: 初，陝西巡撫布喀劾四川陝西總督吳赫等侵蝕貧民籽粒銀兩，命鵬翮與傅臘塔往按。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shaanxi Governor Buka had impeached Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Wu He and others for embezzling the seed-grain silver of poor people; Penghe and Fulate were ordered to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shaanxi Governor Buka had charged Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Wu He and others with embezzling poor people's seed-grain silver; Penghe and Fulate were sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 還奏未稱旨，命鵬翮與傅臘塔復往陝西詳審。

translations.literal: Their report on return did not please the emperor; Penghe and Fulate were ordered to go again to Shaanxi for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: Their report displeased the emperor; Penghe and Fulate were sent back to Shaanxi for a fuller inquiry.

sentences.zh: 三十九年春，還奏布喀、吳赫及知州藺佳選、知縣張鳴遠等侵蝕挪用，各擬罪如律。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-ninth year they returned and reported that Buka, Wu He, Prefect Lan Jiaxuan, Magistrate Zhang Mingyuan, and others had embezzled and diverted funds; each was sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year thirty-nine (1700) they reported that Buka, Wu He, Prefect Lan Jiaxuan, Magistrate Zhang Mingyuan, and others had embezzled and misused funds; each was sentenced under law.

sentences.zh: 上諭大學士曰：「鵬翮往陝西，朕留心訪察，一介不取，天下廉吏無出其右。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the grand secretaries: "When Penghe went to Shaanxi, I kept watch in inquiry—he took not a single thing; among honest officials under heaven none ranks above him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the grand secretaries, "When Penghe went to Shaanxi I made careful inquiry: he took not a single thing; among honest officials under heaven none ranks above him.

sentences.zh: 尋授河道總督，入辭，上諭令毀攔黃壩通下流，濬芒稻河、人字河湖入江。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director-General of Rivers; on taking leave to enter office the emperor instructed him to destroy the Yellow-blocking dam to open the lower course, and to dredge the Mangdao River and the ren-shaped lake-river so they entered the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made river director; at his farewell audience the emperor ordered him to tear down the Yellow-blocking dam to free the lower course and dredge the Mangdao River and the ren-shaped channel into the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮到官，請撤協理徐廷璽及河工隨帶人員，並乞敕工部毋以不應查駁之事阻撓，並從之。

translations.literal: When Penghe reached his post he asked to remove co-supervisor Xu Tingxi and the personnel attached to river works, and also begged an imperial order that the Ministry of Works not obstruct him with matters that ought not to be audited and rejected; all was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Penghe asked to remove co-supervisor Xu Tingxi and extra river staff, and begged an edict that the Ministry of Works not block him with petty audits; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「臣過雲梯關，見攔黃壩巍然如山，下流不暢，無怪上流之潰決。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: "When your servant passed Yunti Pass, I saw the Yellow-blocking dam towering like a mountain; the lower course was not free—no wonder the upper course burst.
translations.idiomatic: He soon wrote, "At Yunti Pass I found the Yellow-blocking dam piled like a mountain; the lower course was choked—no wonder the upper reaches kept breaking.

sentences.zh: 應拆攔黃壩，挑濬河身，與上流一律寬深。

translations.literal: The Yellow-blocking dam should be torn down, the river bed dredged, and made uniformly wide and deep like the upper course.
translations.idiomatic: The dam should come down, the channel be dredged, and the bed made as wide and deep as the upper reach.

sentences.zh: 」又言清口淤墊，應於張福口開引河，引清水入運敵黃，建閘以時啟閉。

translations.literal: " He also said that Qingkou was silted and filled in, that a diversion channel should be opened at Zhangfukou to draw clear water into the Grand Canal to contend with the Yellow River, and that sluice gates should be built to open and close in season.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said Qingkou was silted shut, that a diversion should be cut at Zhangfukou to bring clear water into the canal against the Yellow River, with timed sluice gates.

sentences.zh: 又言人字河至芒稻山分二派，又名芒稻河，應濬使暢流；

translations.literal: He also said that the ren-shaped river divided into two branches at Mangdao Hill, also called the Mangdao River, and should be dredged for free flow;
translations.idiomatic: He also said the ren-shaped river split in two at Mangdao Hill—the Mangdao River—and should be dredged for a free current;

sentences.zh: 並濬鳳凰橋引河及雙橋、灣頭二河，皆匯芒稻河入江。

translations.literal: and that the diversion at Fenghuang Bridge and the two rivers at Shuangqiao and Wantou should also be dredged, all joining the Mangdao River to enter the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: and that the Fenghuang Bridge diversion and the Shuangqiao and Wantou channels should be dredged as well, all feeding the Mangdao into the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 俱下部議行。

translations.literal: All were sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All went to the ministries for approval and action.

sentences.zh: 尋以攔黃壩既撤，河身開濬深通，暢流入海，疏請賜名大通口。

translations.literal: Soon, because the Yellow-blocking dam had been removed and the river bed dredged deep and clear so that water flowed freely to the sea, he memorialized asking that the place be granted the name Datong Estuary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow-blocking dam was gone and the channel dredged deep so water ran freely to the sea, he asked that the mouth be named Datong Estuary.

sentences.zh: 上嘉鵬翮章奏詞簡意明，治事精詳，遣員外郎拖抗拖和、中書張古禮馳驛令鵬翮舉所規畫入奏。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Penghe's memorials as concise in wording and clear in meaning and his handling of affairs as meticulous; he sent Director Tuokang Tuohe and Secretariat Drafter Zhang Guli by post relay to order Penghe to report all his plans.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Penghe's memorials as clear and his work as meticulous, and sent Director Tuokang Tuohe and Drafter Zhang Guli by express post to have him report his full plan.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮疏陳開濬引河、運口，培修河岸堤壩諸事，並下部速議行。

translations.literal: Penghe memorialized on dredging diversion channels and the canal mouth, repairing river banks, dikes, and dams, and other matters; all were sent to the ministries for swift deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe laid out dredging diversions and the canal mouth, bank repairs, and dike work; all were sent to the ministries for swift action.

sentences.zh: 尋又疏陳河工諸弊，並請河員承挑引河，偶致淤墊，免其賠修；

translations.literal: Soon he again memorialized on abuses in river works, and also asked that when river officials undertook diversion channels and siltation occurred by chance, they be exempted from paying for repairs;
translations.idiomatic: He soon exposed abuses in river administration and asked that officials who dug diversion channels not be forced to pay for accidental silting;

sentences.zh: 夫役勞苦，工成日請給印票免雜徭。

translations.literal: and that laborers, worn with toil, on the day works were finished should be given sealed passes exempting them from miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: and that worn-out laborers receive sealed passes on completion day exempting them from miscellaneous corvée.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其陳奏切要周備。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his memorials as urgent in point and thorough in completeness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorials as timely and thorough.

sentences.zh: 尋又請於歸仁堤五堡建磯心石閘，並於三義壩舊中河築堤，改入新中河，合為一河，便糧艘通行。

translations.literal: Soon he again asked to build stone sluices with rock cores at the five forts of the Guiren dike, and to build a dike at the old Middle River at Sanyi Dam to divert into the new Middle River, joining them into one river for the convenience of grain transports.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked for rock-core stone sluices at the five forts of the Guiren dike, and a dike at Sanyi Dam to shift the old Middle River into the new channel so grain boats could pass in one stream.

sentences.zh: 上謂所議甚當，並如所請。

translations.literal: The emperor said the proposals were very fitting, and all were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called the plan sound and granted everything he asked.

sentences.zh: 上倚鵬翮治河，謂鵬翮得治河秘要，諭大學士曰：「鵬翮自到河工，日乘馬巡視堤岸，不憚勞苦。

translations.literal: The emperor relied on Penghe to manage the rivers, saying Penghe had grasped the secret essentials of river control, and instructed the grand secretaries: "Since Penghe reached the river works he has ridden out daily to inspect the dikes, not fearing hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relied on Penghe for river control, said he had mastered its secrets, and told the grand secretaries, "Since Penghe took the post he has ridden the dikes every day without flinching from hardship.

sentences.zh: 居官如鵬翮，更有何議？

translations.literal: If one serves in office like Penghe, what more is there to debate?
translations.idiomatic: With an official like Penghe, what more is there to debate?

sentences.zh: 」鵬翮以修治事狀遣郎中王進楫入奏，上諭進楫歸語鵬翮，加意防守高家堰。

translations.literal: " Penghe sent Director Wang Jinji to report on the state of repairs; the emperor instructed Jinji to return and tell Penghe to give special attention to defending Gaojiayan.
translations.idiomatic: " Penghe sent Director Wang Jinji to report on repairs; the emperor told Jinji to tell Penghe to guard Gaojiayan with extra care.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮乃增築月堤及旁近諸堤壩。

translations.literal: Penghe then raised crescent dikes and the nearby dikes and dams.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe then raised crescent dikes and the neighboring embankments.

sentences.zh: 洪澤湖溢，泗州、盱眙被災，上詢修治策，鵬翮言：「泗州、盱眙屢被災，即開六壩亦不能免。

translations.literal: When Hongze Lake overflowed and Sizhou and Xuyi suffered disaster, the emperor asked for repair policy; Penghe said: "Sizhou and Xuyi have often suffered disaster; even if the six dams were opened they could not be spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongze Lake spilled over and Sizhou and Xuyi were flooded, the emperor asked for a remedy; Penghe said, "Sizhou and Xuyi flood again and again—even opening the six spillway dams would not save them.

sentences.zh: 」上怒曰：「塞六壩乃於成龍題請，不自鵬翮始。

translations.literal: " The emperor angrily said: "Sealing the six dams was proposed on Chenglong's memorial; it did not begin with Penghe.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor snapped, "Closing the six dams was Chenglong's proposal—not Penghe's.

sentences.zh: 頃因泗州、盱眙災，令與阿山議修治，非欲開六壩救泗州、盱眙而令淮、揚罹水患也。

translations.literal: Just now, because of disaster at Sizhou and Xuyi, I ordered discussion with Ashan on repairs—I did not mean to open the six dams to save Sizhou and Xuyi while letting Huai and Yang suffer flood.
translations.idiomatic: I sent you and Ashan to discuss repairs for Sizhou and Xuyi—not to open the six dams and drown Huai and Yang to save those two towns.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮何昏憒乃爾！

translations.literal: How can Penghe be so muddled and foolish!
translations.idiomatic: How can Penghe be so muddled!

sentences.zh: 」四十一年，鵬翮疏請加築清河縣黃河南北岸戧堤，天妃閘改築運口，草壩建石壩，改卞家莊土堤為石堤，皆議行。

translations.literal: " In the forty-first year Penghe memorialized asking to raise battle dikes on the north and south banks of the Yellow River in Qinghe County, rebuild the canal mouth at the Tianfei Sluice, build a stone dam at the grass dam, and change the earthen dike at Bianjiazhuang to stone; all were deliberated and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " In year forty-one (1702) Penghe asked to raise battle dikes on the Yellow River banks in Qinghe County, rebuild the canal mouth at Tianfei Sluice, face the grass dam in stone, and stone-face the dike at Bianjiazhuang; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 又以桃源城西煙墩黃水大漲，請加築衛城月堤，並於邵家莊、顏家莊開引河，上慮部議遲延，特允之。

translations.literal: Because the Yellow River rose greatly at Yandun west of Taoyuan city, he also asked to raise the crescent dike of the garrison city and open diversion channels at Shaojiazhuang and Yanjiazhuang; the emperor feared ministry deliberation would delay matters and specially approved them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River surged at Yandun west of Taoyuan, he asked for a crescent dike around the garrison city and diversions at Shaojiazhuang and Yanjiazhuang; fearing ministry delay, the emperor approved at once.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，上南巡視河，制河臣箴、淮黃告成詩以賜，並書榜賚鵬翮父良。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year the emperor toured the south to inspect the rivers, composed an Admonition for River Officials and a poem on the completion of the Huai and Yellow, and granted them; he also wrote an inscribed board and bestowed it on Penghe's father Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-two (1703) the emperor toured the south to inspect the rivers, composed an Admonition for River Officials and a poem on the Huai and Yellow works completed, and gave them to Penghe; he also wrote an inscribed board for Penghe's father Liang.

sentences.zh: 山東泰安、沂州等州飢，上命截漕二萬石交鵬翮往賑。

translations.literal: Famine struck Taian, Yizhou, and other prefectures in Shandong; the emperor ordered twenty thousand shi of grain transport diverted and given to Penghe for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Taian, Yizhou, and other Shandong prefectures faced famine; the emperor diverted twenty thousand shi of tribute grain to Penghe for relief.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮令河員動常平倉穀二十八萬餘石散賑，疏請以山東各官俸工補還。

translations.literal: Penghe ordered river officials to move more than two hundred eighty thousand shi of grain from the ever-normal granaries for relief distribution, and memorialized asking that Shandong officials make repayment from salary and labor allotments.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe had river officials release more than 280,000 shi from ever-normal granaries for relief, then asked Shandong officials to repay it from salary and labor funds.

sentences.zh: 上責鵬翮河員發倉穀邀譽，乃令山東各官補還，鵬翮謝罪，仍以「殫心宣力、清潔自持」，加太子太保。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Penghe because river officials had released granary grain to win praise; he nevertheless ordered Shandong officials to repay it; Penghe begged forgiveness, and was still advanced to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the commendation "exhausting heart and strength in service, holding himself pure and clean."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Penghe for letting river officials raid the granaries for credit, yet still ordered Shandong officials to repay; Penghe apologized and was still made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the praise "devoted in service, pure in conduct."

sentences.zh: 河決時家馬頭，數年未堵塞。

translations.literal: The river breached at Shijia Matou; for several years it was not sealed.
translations.idiomatic: The river had breached at Shijia Matou and remained open for years.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮以淮安道王謙言劾山安同知佟世祿冒帑誤工，奪官追償。

translations.literal: On the word of Huai'an Circuit intendant Wang Qianyan, Penghe impeached Shan'an Assistant Prefect Tong Shilu for falsely drawing treasury funds and bungling the work; his office was stripped and repayment ordered.
translations.idiomatic: On Huai'an intendant Wang Qianyan's report, Penghe impeached Shan'an assistant prefect Tong Shilu for embezzling funds and botching the work; Tong lost his post and was ordered to repay.

sentences.zh: 世祿再叩閽，上令尚書徐潮按治，鵬翮、謙坐誣劾當譴，上特寬鵬翮。

translations.literal: Shilu again knocked at the palace gate; the emperor ordered Minister Xu Chao to investigate; Penghe and Qian were liable to punishment for false impeachment, but the emperor specially showed leniency to Penghe.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu petitioned at the palace gate again; Minister Xu Chao was sent to investigate; Penghe and Qian were liable for false impeachment, but the emperor spared Penghe.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎趙世芳又劾鵬翮浮銷十三萬有奇，請逮治。

translations.literal: Works Vice Minister Zhao Shifang again impeached Penghe for inflated expenditure of more than one hundred thirty thousand taels and asked that he be arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Works Vice Minister Zhao Shifang then charged Penghe with padding accounts by more than 130,000 taels and asked for his arrest.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「河工錢糧原不限數，水大所需多，水小所需少。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "River-work funds and grain were never limited in amount; when the water is great more is needed, when the water is small less is needed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "River funds were never capped—high water demands more, low water less.

sentences.zh: 如謂鵬翮以十三萬入己，必無之事。

translations.literal: To say that Penghe put one hundred thirty thousand into his own pocket—that certainly did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: To say Penghe pocketed 130,000 taels—that simply did not happen.

sentences.zh: 河工恃用人，鵬翮用人不勝事，故至此耳。

translations.literal: River works depend on men employed; Penghe's men could not bear the tasks—hence it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: River work lives or dies on the men you hire; Penghe's men could not carry the load—that is how it came to this."

sentences.zh: 」因還世芳疏。

translations.literal: The memorial was returned to Shifang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned Shifang’s memorial.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，閱清口，見黃水倒灌，詰鵬翮，鵬翮不能對。

translations.literal: On his southern tour the emperor inspected Qingkou, saw Yellow River water backing up, questioned Penghe, and Penghe could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: On his southern tour the emperor inspected Qingkou, saw the Yellow River backing in, questioned Penghe, and Penghe had no reply.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝為王謙輩所欺，流於刻薄。

translations.literal: The emperor said: “You have been deceived by Wang Qian and his like and have grown harsh and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: “Wang Qian and his sort have misled you—you have grown harsh and petty.

sentences.zh: 大儒持身如光風霽月，況大臣為國，若徒自表廉潔，於事何益？

translations.literal: A great scholar conducts himself like clear wind after rain; how much more should a minister serving the state—if he merely displays his own integrity and frugality, what good does that do the work?
translations.idiomatic: A great scholar’s bearing is open as sky after rain; how much more a minister serving the state—mere display of personal integrity helps the work not at all.

sentences.zh: 」上舟渡河閱九里岡，嘉鵬翮修治如法，御製詩書扇以賜。

translations.literal: The emperor took a boat across the river to inspect Jiuligang, praised Penghe’s repairs as conforming to proper method, and bestowed a fan with an imperial poem.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed by boat to inspect Jiuligang, praised Penghe’s repairs as sound practice, and gave him a fan inscribed with an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 及秋，淮、黃並漲，古溝、清水溝、韓家莊並溢，廷臣議奪官，上命仍留任。

translations.literal: By autumn the Huai and Yellow both rose; Gugou, Qingshuigou, and Hanjiazhuang all overflowed; court ministers deliberated stripping his office, but the emperor ordered him kept in post.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Huai and Yellow waters rose together; Gugou, Qingshuigou, and Hanjiazhuang all failed; ministers urged dismissal, but the emperor kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 尋督塞諸處漫口。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he supervised sealing the overflow openings at various places.
translations.idiomatic: He soon oversaw plugging breaches along the line.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，疏請開鮑家營引河，尋用通判徐光啟言，擬開引河出張福口，分​​洪澤湖異漲，即為高家堰保障，謂為溜淮套。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he memorialized requesting opening a diversion at Baojiaying; shortly afterward, adopting Sub-Prefect Xu Guangqi’s advice, he proposed opening a diversion channel at Zhangfukou to divide Hongze Lake’s abnormal floods, thereby protecting Gaojiayan—called the “Huai-diversion channel.”
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year (1706) he asked to open a diversion at Baojiaying; soon adopting Sub-Prefect Xu Guangqi’s plan, he proposed a channel at Zhangfukou to split Hongze’s flood surges and shield Gaojiayan—the “Huai-diversion channel.”

sentences.zh: 鵬翮與總督阿山、總漕桑額合疏請上蒞視。

translations.literal: Penghe, together with Governor-General Ashan and Transport Director Sange, jointly memorialized asking the emperor to come in person to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe, Governor-General Ashan, and Transport Director Sange jointly asked the emperor to inspect in person.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，上南巡，閱所擬引河道，諭曰：「朕自清口至曹家廟，見地勢甚高，標竿錯雜。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, on his southern tour, the emperor inspected the proposed diversion route and instructed: “From Qingkou to Caojiamiao I saw the terrain is very high and the survey stakes are jumbled.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year (1707), on his southern tour, he inspected the proposed channel and said: “From Qingkou to Caojiamiao the ground is very high and the survey stakes are a mess.

sentences.zh: 依此開河，不惟壞田產，抑且毀塚墓。

translations.literal: If a river is opened on this plan, not only will farmland be ruined, but graves will also be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Cut a river here and you ruin not only fields but graves as well.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮讀書人，乃為此殘忍事，讀書何為？

translations.literal: Penghe is a man of learning—yet he would do this cruel thing; what is reading books for?
translations.idiomatic: Penghe is a scholar—yet he would do this cruel work; what was all his reading for?

sentences.zh: 」詰責鵬翮，鵬翮謝罪。

translations.literal: He rebuked Penghe; Penghe begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked Penghe, who apologized.

sentences.zh: 上以議為河山所主，非鵬翮意，削太子太保，奪官，仍留任。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the plan was dominated by the river and mountain officials, not Penghe’s own intent; he stripped him of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and his office, but kept him at his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed the plan on river officials, not Penghe’s intent; he stripped Senior Guardian rank and office but kept him at work.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，以黃、運、湖、河修防平穩，命复官，並免應追帑銀。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, because Yellow, Transport, lake, and river repairs were stable, his office was restored and recoverable treasury silver was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year (1708), with Yellow, canal, lake, and river defenses stable, his rank was restored and outstanding treasury claims waived.

sentences.zh: 尋遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was shifted to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year (1709) he moved to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，江南總督噶禮與巡撫張伯行互劾，命鵬翮與總漕赫壽往按。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year Jiangnan Governor-General Gali and Governor Zhang Boxing impeached each other; Penghe and Transport Director He Shou were ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year (1712) Governor-General Gali and Governor Zhang Boxing impeached each other; Penghe and Transport Director He Shou were sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮等右噶禮，請罷伯行。

translations.literal: Penghe and the others sided with Gali and asked that Boxing be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe’s party favored Gali and asked to remove Boxing.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year (1713) he moved to the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 伯行劾布政使牟欽元，赫壽時為總督，與異議。

translations.literal: Boxing impeached Administration Commissioner Mou Qinyuan; He Shou was then governor-general and disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing impeached Administration Commissioner Mou Qinyuan; Governor-General He Shou dissented.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，命鵬翮與副都御史阿錫鼐往按，復請雪欽元，議伯行罪斬。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year Penghe and Vice Censor-in-Chief Axidai were ordered to investigate; they again asked to clear Qinyuan and recommended execution for Boxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year (1714) Penghe and Vice Censor-in-Chief Axidai reinvestigated, again cleared Qinyuan, and recommended Boxing for execution.

sentences.zh: 事互詳伯行傳。

translations.literal: The matter is cross-referenced in Boxing’s biography.
translations.idiomatic: See Zhang Boxing’s biography for the full account.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂，以原官回籍守制，服闋還朝。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he entered mourning for his father, returned home at his former rank to observe mourning, and after the mourning period returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He soon mourned his father, returned home at his former rank, and came back to court when mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 六十年，汶水旱涸阻運，命往勘。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year drought dried the Wen River and blocked transport; he was ordered to survey.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year (1721) drought dried the Wen River and blocked transport; he was ordered to survey.

sentences.zh: 請疏濬坎河、雞爪諸泉分注南旺，而於彭口築堤，障沙水入微山湖。

translations.literal: He asked to dredge the Kan River and springs such as Jizhua to feed Nanwang, and to build a dike at Pengkou to block sandy water entering Weishan Lake.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed dredging the Kan River and Jizhua springs into Nanwang and building a dike at Pengkou to keep sandy water out of Weishan Lake.

sentences.zh: 河決開州，橫流至山東張秋，阻運，命往勘。

translations.literal: The river breached at Kaizhou and flowed across to Zhangqiu in Shandong, blocking transport; he was ordered to survey.
translations.idiomatic: The river burst at Kaizhou and flooded across to Zhangqiu in Shandong, blocking transport; he was sent to survey again.

sentences.zh: 請築南旺、馬場等湖堤，蓄水濟運；

translations.literal: He asked to build dikes at Nanwang, Machang, and other lakes to store water for transport;
translations.idiomatic: He asked to build dikes at Nanwang, Machang, and other lakes to store water for the transport route;

sentences.zh: 並陳引沁入運利害，謂地勢西北高於東南，若沁水從高直下，而河躡其後，害且叵測。

translations.literal: and also set forth the advantages and disadvantages of diverting the Qin into the transport route, saying the terrain is higher in the northwest than the southeast—if Qin water plunged down from above with the Yellow River pressing behind, the harm would be beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: and argued against diverting the Qin into the canal: the northwest lies higher than the southeast—if Qin water plunged downhill with the Yellow River pressing behind, the harm would be incalculable.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，世宗即位，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, when the Shizong acceded, he was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year (1722), when the Yongzheng Emperor acceded, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，授武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng (1723) he became Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 河決馬營口，久未塞，命往勘。

translations.literal: The river breached at Mayingkou and long went unsealed; he was ordered to survey.
translations.idiomatic: The river burst at Mayingkou and long remained open; he was sent to survey.

sentences.zh: 議並塞詹家店四口，濬治黃、沁合流處積沙，從之。

translations.literal: He proposed sealing the four openings at Zhanjiadian together and dredging accumulated sand where the Yellow and Qin meet; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed sealing four breaches at Zhanjiadian and dredging silt where Yellow and Qin meet; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，加少保，命於定例外加祭，漢堂上官、科道皆會賜葬，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; he was given Junior Guardian, ordered funeral sacrifices beyond the regulation, Han officials of rank and censors all joined in granting burial honors, and posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1725) he died; he was made Junior Guardian, granted extraordinary funeral rites, and given the posthumous title Wenduan (“Cultured and Upright”).

sentences.zh: 論曰：明治河諸臣，推潘季馴為最，蓋借黃以濟運，又藉淮以刷黃，固非束水攻沙不可也。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Among river-control ministers of the Ming, Pan Jixun is ranked highest, for he used the Yellow to aid transport and the Huai to scour the Yellow—truly one cannot do without confining water to attack sand.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Among Ming river ministers Pan Jixun stands highest—using the Yellow to serve transport and the Huai to scour the Yellow; confining water to attack sand was indispensable.

sentences.zh: 方興、之錫皆守其成法，而輔尤以是底績。

translations.literal: Fangxing and Zhixi both kept to his established methods, and Fu especially achieved lasting results thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Fangxing and Zhixi followed his established methods; Fu above all achieved lasting results that way.

sentences.zh: 輔八疏以濬下流為第一，節費不得已而議減水。

translations.literal: Fu’s eight memorials put dredging the lower reach first; economizing funds left no choice but to propose flood-relief dams.
translations.idiomatic: Fu’s eight memorials made dredging the lower reach the first priority; saving funds forced him to rely on relief dams.

sentences.zh: 成龍主治海口，及躬其任，仍不廢減水策。

translations.literal: Chenglong chiefly advocated opening the sea mouth; yet when he personally held office he still did not abandon the relief-dam policy.
translations.idiomatic: Chenglong chiefly favored opening the estuary; yet in office he never abandoned relief dams.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮承上指，大通口工成，入海道始暢。

translations.literal: Penghe followed the emperor’s direction; when the Datong Estuary works were completed, the route to the sea was at last open.
translations.idiomatic: Penghe followed the emperor’s lead; when the Datong Estuary project was done, the sea route at last ran clear.

sentences.zh: 然終不能用輔初議，大舉濬治。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Fu’s original proposal for large-scale dredging could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fu’s original plan for large-scale dredging was never fully carried out.

sentences.zh: 世以開中河、培高家堰為輔功，孰知輔言固未盡用也。

translations.literal: The world credits opening the Middle River and heightening Gaojiayan as Fu’s achievements—who knows that Fu’s words were in fact not fully employed?
translations.idiomatic: Posterity credits the Middle River and Gaojiayan embankment to Fu—yet his larger vision was never fully adopted.
